It is usually best to avoid sex during treatment, since boric acid can irritate a partner and oral contact should be avoided.
Why is boric acid used for yeast infections?
It can help when yeast keeps coming back or is a type that doesn't respond well to usual antifungal medicines. This use is off-label.

name: Brimonidine
uses: Facial redness from rosacea.
how: Narrows blood vessels in the skin to reduce redness.
avoid: Use as directed; overuse can cause rebound redness.
about: Brimonidine is an alpha-2 agonist first used as an eye drop for glaucoma and later as a gel for the facial redness of rosacea. It narrows the small blood vessels in the skin, which can temporarily reduce redness. Dermatologists may ask for it compounded in a cream, sometimes combined with ivermectin, azelaic acid or oxymetazoline to treat more than one rosacea symptom at once.
serious: Get medical help right away for signs of an allergic reaction, such as swelling of the face or trouble breathing, or for fainting, severe dizziness or a very slow heartbeat.
interactions: Use care with MAO inhibitors, some antidepressants, blood pressure and heart medicines, and alcohol or sedatives. Give your prescriber a full list of medicines and supplements.
pregnancy: There is limited information on topical brimonidine in pregnancy or breastfeeding; talk to your prescriber if you are pregnant, planning pregnancy or breastfeeding.
tips: Apply a thin, even layer to the face, avoiding the eyes, lips and inside of the nose.
Use it only as often as directed, since overuse can lead to rebound redness.
Wash your hands right after applying so you don't rub it in your eyes.
monitoring: Routine monitoring is usually not needed, but keep follow-up visits your prescriber schedules.
faqs: How quickly does brimonidine reduce redness?
Redness often decreases within about half an hour and the effect lasts for several hours, then wears off.
What is rebound redness?
Some people notice redness returning stronger than before as the medicine wears off. Using it only as directed can help, and tell your prescriber if it happens.

name: Budesonide
uses: Inflammatory bowel disease and other inflammation, with fewer whole-body steroid effects.
side: Increased thirst and appetite, mild steroid effects.
how: A steroid that acts mainly in the gut and is largely broken down by the liver before reaching the rest of the body.
avoid: People or pets with liver disease or active infections.
about: Budesonide is a corticosteroid used since the 1990s for asthma, nasal allergies and gut inflammation. When taken by mouth, much of it is broken down by the liver before reaching the rest of the body, so it may cause fewer whole-body steroid effects. Veterinarians use it off-label in dogs and cats with inflammatory bowel disease, and compounding gives smaller capsule strengths or a flavored suspension.
conditions: Inflammatory bowel disease in dogs and cats
serious: Get medical or veterinary help right away for signs of infection such as fever or chills, severe weakness or dizziness, vision changes, black or bloody stools, or yellowing of the skin, gums or eyes.
interactions: Ketoconazole, itraconazole, clarithromycin, some HIV medicines and grapefruit juice can greatly raise budesonide levels, and other steroids add to its effects. Give your prescriber, or your pet's veterinarian, a full list of medicines, supplements and flea or tick products.
pregnancy: Talk to your prescriber if you are pregnant, planning pregnancy or breastfeeding; budesonide may be used when the benefit outweighs the risk.
petNotes: Budesonide can still cause steroid effects in pets, such as more thirst, urination and appetite, especially in dogs. Capsules should not be crushed or opened unless your veterinarian or pharmacist says so, since some are designed to release in the gut.
tips: Take or give it in the morning unless directed otherwise.
Swallow capsules whole if instructed; don't crush or chew them.
Avoid grapefruit and grapefruit juice.
Don't stop it suddenly after long use; your prescriber or veterinarian will explain how to taper.
monitoring: Your prescriber or veterinarian may check blood sugar, bone health with long use, or adrenal function, and will follow up on symptoms.
faqs: Is budesonide safer than prednisone?
Budesonide is designed to act mainly in the gut, so it may cause fewer whole-body steroid effects. It is still a steroid, and your prescriber decides which is right.
Can budesonide be used for my dog's IBD?
Veterinarians use it off-label in dogs and cats with inflammatory bowel disease, especially when prednisone causes side effects.

name: Bupropion
uses: Depression and smoking cessation.
side: Dry mouth, trouble sleeping, headache, anxiety.
how: Increases dopamine and norepinephrine in the brain.
avoid: People with seizure disorders or eating disorders, and anyone stopping alcohol or sedatives abruptly.
about: Bupropion is an antidepressant introduced in the late 1980s that works differently from SSRIs by acting on dopamine and norepinephrine. It is prescribed for depression, seasonal depression and to help people quit smoking. It is less likely than many antidepressants to cause sexual side effects or drowsiness. Compounded capsules may be used when a prescriber needs a strength or combination not sold commercially.
serious: Get medical help right away for a seizure, new or worsening thoughts of suicide or unusual mood changes, a severe rash or swelling, eye pain or vision changes, or very high blood pressure.
interactions: Never combine it with MAO inhibitors, and use care with medicines that lower the seizure threshold such as some antipsychotics, theophylline, steroids and some opioid pain medicines, as well as alcohol; it can also raise levels of some heart and antidepressant medicines. Give your prescriber a full list of medicines and supplements.
pregnancy: Talk to your prescriber if you are pregnant, planning pregnancy or breastfeeding; bupropion may be continued when the benefit outweighs the risk.
tips: Take it in the morning if it keeps you awake at night.
Swallow capsules whole if directed; don't crush or chew long-acting forms.
Limit or avoid alcohol, which raises seizure risk.
If you miss a dose, take it when you remember unless it is almost time for the next one; don't double up.
monitoring: Your prescriber will follow your mood and may check blood pressure periodically.
faqs: How long does bupropion take to work?
Some people notice changes in energy within a week or two, but full benefit for mood often takes several weeks.
Can I drink alcohol while taking bupropion?
It is best to limit or avoid alcohol. Drinking heavily, or suddenly stopping after heavy drinking, can raise the risk of seizures.
Does bupropion cause sexual side effects?
It is less likely than many other antidepressants to cause sexual side effects, though everyone responds differently.

name: Buspirone
uses: Anxiety in people; anxiety and urine marking in cats.
how: Acts on serotonin receptors to reduce anxiety without heavy sedation.
avoid: Anyone taking MAO inhibitors, and people with severe liver or kidney disease.
about: Buspirone is an anti-anxiety medicine introduced in the 1980s that acts on serotonin receptors. Unlike many anxiety medicines, it is not habit-forming and usually doesn't cause heavy sedation. Veterinarians use it off-label in cats for anxiety and urine marking and sometimes in dogs. Compounded liquids and transdermal gels help when pets need small amounts or won't take pills.
serious: Get medical or veterinary help right away for chest pain, fainting, signs of an allergic reaction, or agitation with fever, sweating, tremor or a fast heartbeat.
interactions: Never combine it with MAO inhibitors, including selegiline and amitraz in some tick collars, and use care with other serotonin medicines; ketoconazole, itraconazole, erythromycin and grapefruit juice can raise its levels. Give your prescriber, or your pet's veterinarian, a full list of medicines, supplements and flea or tick products.
pregnancy: There is limited information on buspirone in pregnancy and breastfeeding; talk to your prescriber if you are pregnant, planning pregnancy or breastfeeding.
petNotes: In cats it may take a few weeks to see a difference in anxiety or marking, and some cats become more affectionate or, less often, more assertive with other cats. Transdermal gel may be absorbed less reliably than oral forms.
tips: Take it the same way each time, either always with food or always without, since food changes how much is absorbed.
Avoid large amounts of grapefruit juice.
Wear gloves when applying gel to your pet's ear.
If you miss a dose, take it when you remember unless it is almost time for the next one; don't double up.
monitoring: Routine monitoring is usually not needed, but your prescriber or veterinarian will follow up on how well it is working.
faqs: How long does buspirone take to work?
It does not work right away like some anxiety medicines; benefits often build over a few weeks.
Is buspirone addictive?
Buspirone is not considered habit-forming, which is one reason prescribers choose it.
Can buspirone help my cat stop spraying?
Veterinarians sometimes use it off-label for urine marking in cats, along with checking for medical causes and changes at home.

name: Cabergoline
uses: High prolactin in people; false pregnancy and some reproductive uses in dogs.
how: Stimulates dopamine receptors to lower prolactin.
avoid: Pregnant pets (unless intended), and people with heart valve disease or uncontrolled blood pressure.
about: Cabergoline is a long-acting dopamine agonist used since the 1990s to lower prolactin, a hormone made by the pituitary gland. In people it treats high prolactin, often from a small pituitary tumor. Veterinarians use it off-label in dogs for false pregnancy and some reproductive purposes. Since dogs need tiny, precise amounts, it is often compounded as a flavored oral suspension.
serious: Get medical or veterinary help right away for shortness of breath, chest pain, swelling of the legs, a persistent cough, fainting, severe vomiting, or uncontrollable urges such as gambling in people.
interactions: Medicines that block dopamine, such as antipsychotics and metoclopramide, work against it, and some macrolide antibiotics may raise its levels. Give your prescriber, or your pet's veterinarian, a full list of medicines, supplements and flea or tick products.
pregnancy: Talk to your prescriber if you are pregnant or planning pregnancy, and don't use it while breastfeeding, since it stops milk production.
petNotes: Giving it with food may reduce vomiting in dogs. Because it can end a pregnancy, it should not be given to pregnant dogs unless your veterinarian intends that.
tips: Take or give it with food to lower nausea.
Shake the suspension well before measuring.
Get up slowly if you feel dizzy.
If you miss a dose, take it when you remember unless it is almost time for the next one; don't double up.
monitoring: Your prescriber may check prolactin levels and, with long-term use, heart valve health with an echocardiogram.
faqs: Can cabergoline stop breast milk?
Yes, cabergoline lowers prolactin and can stop milk production, so it is not used while breastfeeding.
How is cabergoline used for false pregnancy in dogs?
Veterinarians may use it off-label to lower prolactin, which can reduce milk production and nesting behavior. Your veterinarian decides the plan.

name: Caffeine
uses: Ingredient in topical hair-growth serums.
how: Stimulates hair follicles when applied to the scalp.
avoid: Usually well tolerated topically. Toxic to pets if swallowed.
about: Caffeine is a natural stimulant best known from coffee and tea. In topical form, it is added to hair serums because lab studies suggest it may stimulate hair follicles and counter some effects of hormones linked to hair thinning. Prescribers may combine it in a compounded scalp serum with ingredients such as niacinamide, ketoconazole or tretinoin as part of a hair care plan.
serious: Get medical help right away for signs of an allergic reaction, such as hives, swelling or trouble breathing. If a pet licks or swallows the serum, call your veterinarian or a pet poison helpline.
interactions: Very little caffeine is absorbed from a scalp serum, so drug interactions are unlikely. Give your prescriber a full list of medicines and supplements.
pregnancy: Little caffeine is absorbed from the scalp, but check with your prescriber before using it with other serum ingredients if you are pregnant, planning pregnancy or breastfeeding.
tips: Apply to a clean, dry scalp and massage gently.
Let it dry before styling or lying on a pillow, and wash your hands after applying.
Keep the bottle away from pets.
Hair changes take months, so use it steadily as directed.
monitoring: Routine monitoring is usually not needed, but keep follow-up visits your prescriber schedules.
faqs: Does topical caffeine keep you awake?
Very little caffeine is absorbed through the scalp, so it is not expected to act like drinking coffee.
How long until I see results from a caffeine hair serum?
Hair grows slowly, so it usually takes a few months of regular use to judge any change.

name: Calcipotriene
uses: Psoriasis and some skin growths.
how: A vitamin D analog that slows skin cell overgrowth.
avoid: People with high calcium. Toxic to pets.
about: Calcipotriene is a topical form of vitamin D that has been used on the skin since the 1990s to treat psoriasis. It slows the overgrowth of skin cells that causes thick, scaly patches. Dermatologists may use it in compounded creams, sometimes combined with fluorouracil, off-label, to treat certain precancerous skin growths. Compounding allows a custom base or combination.
serious: Get medical help right away for signs of high calcium, such as extreme thirst, frequent urination, confusion, constipation, muscle weakness or nausea, or for severe skin irritation or an allergic reaction.
interactions: Salicylic acid can inactivate calcipotriene if mixed on the skin, and calcium or vitamin D supplements and thiazide diuretics may add to calcium effects with heavy use. Give your prescriber a full list of medicines and supplements.
pregnancy: There is limited information on calcipotriene in pregnancy or breastfeeding; talk to your prescriber if you are pregnant, planning pregnancy or breastfeeding.
tips: Apply a thin layer only to affected areas and avoid the face unless directed.
Wash your hands after applying.
Limit sun and tanning beds on treated skin.
Keep the tube away from pets; swallowing even a small amount can be deadly to dogs and cats.
monitoring: Routine monitoring is usually not needed for typical use, but your prescriber may check calcium if you use large amounts or have kidney problems.
faqs: How long does calcipotriene take to work for psoriasis?
Many people see improvement after a few weeks of regular use.
Why is calcipotriene dangerous for pets?
Dogs and cats who chew or lick the tube can get dangerously high calcium, which can damage the kidneys and heart. Call your veterinarian or a pet poison helpline right away if this happens.

name: Calcitriol
uses: Active vitamin D for calcium balance in kidney disease and low parathyroid function.
how: The active form of vitamin D, which helps the body absorb calcium and controls parathyroid hormone.
avoid: People or pets with high calcium or high phosphorus.
about: Calcitriol is the active form of vitamin D, normally made by the kidneys. It has been used since the late 1970s for people whose bodies can't make enough, such as those with kidney disease or low parathyroid function. Veterinarians use it off-label in cats and dogs with kidney disease or low calcium after parathyroid or thyroid surgery. Because pets need tiny amounts, compounded flavored suspensions are often used.
conditions: Kidney disease with high parathyroid hormone
Kidney disease in dogs and cats
Low calcium after parathyroid surgery in pets
serious: Get medical or veterinary help right away for signs of high calcium, such as extreme thirst, frequent urination, vomiting, constipation, weakness, confusion, not eating or an irregular heartbeat.
interactions: Other vitamin D products, calcium supplements and thiazide diuretics can raise calcium, high calcium can make digoxin more dangerous, and some binders such as cholestyramine can reduce absorption. Give your prescriber, or your pet's veterinarian, a full list of medicines, supplements and flea or tick products.
pregnancy: Talk to your prescriber if you are pregnant, planning pregnancy or breastfeeding; calcitriol may be used when needed with careful calcium monitoring.
petNotes: Pets need very small, precise amounts, so shake the suspension well and measure carefully with the syringe provided. Don't add any vitamin D or calcium supplement unless your veterinarian approves it.
tips: Shake the suspension well and use the measuring syringe provided.
Take or give it at the same time each day and follow the diet plan your prescriber or veterinarian recommends.
Avoid other vitamin D and calcium products unless directed.
If you miss a dose, take it when you remember unless it is almost time for the next one; don't double up.
monitoring: Your prescriber or veterinarian will check calcium and phosphorus levels, and often kidney values and parathyroid hormone, regularly.
faqs: What is the difference between calcitriol and regular vitamin D?
Regular vitamin D must be activated by the liver and kidneys, while calcitriol is already the active form. That is why it is used when the kidneys can't do this step.
Why does my pet need blood tests on calcitriol?
Too much can raise calcium to dangerous levels, so regular checks help your veterinarian keep the amount safe.

name: Calcium carbonate
uses: Calcium supplement and phosphate binder.
how: A mineral supplement that also binds phosphorus in food.
avoid: People or pets with high calcium or kidney stones.
about: Calcium carbonate is one of the most common forms of supplemental calcium and has been used for decades as both a mineral supplement and an antacid. Taken with meals, it also binds phosphorus from food so less is absorbed. A flavored liquid can make it easier to give to people who have trouble swallowing tablets and to pets that need a phosphate binder mixed with food.
conditions: Phosphate binding in cats and dogs with kidney disease
serious: Get medical or veterinary help right away for signs of high calcium, such as severe constipation, nausea or vomiting, increased thirst and urination, confusion or unusual weakness.
interactions: Calcium can block absorption of many medicines, including thyroid hormone, iron, tetracycline and fluoroquinolone antibiotics, and some osteoporosis medicines, so doses usually need to be spaced apart. Thiazide diuretics and vitamin D can raise calcium levels further. Give your prescriber, or your pet's veterinarian, a full list of medicines, supplements and flea or tick products.
pregnancy: Calcium is commonly used during pregnancy and breastfeeding, but ask your prescriber how much is right for you and how it fits with your prenatal vitamin.
petNotes: When used as a phosphate binder for pets with kidney disease, it works best mixed into or given with each meal. Your veterinarian may adjust the amount based on blood calcium and phosphorus results.
tips: Take or give it with meals, especially when it is used to bind phosphorus from food.
Shake the suspension well before each dose.
Separate it from other medicines by a few hours unless your prescriber or veterinarian says otherwise.
Drink plenty of water and include fiber in the diet to help prevent constipation.
monitoring: Your prescriber or veterinarian may check blood calcium and phosphorus levels periodically, especially with kidney disease.
faqs: Should calcium carbonate be taken with food?
Yes, it is usually best taken with meals. Food helps absorption, and when it is used as a phosphate binder it needs to be in the stomach with the food to work.
Can calcium carbonate interfere with other medicines?
Yes. It can reduce absorption of thyroid medicine, iron and some antibiotics, so these are usually spaced a few hours apart. Your pharmacist can help you plan the timing.
Can I give my pet calcium carbonate antacid tablets?
Only if your veterinarian recommends it and approves the product. Some flavored or sugar-free human products contain ingredients, such as xylitol, that are dangerous for dogs.

name: Calcium pantothenate
uses: Vitamin B5 supplement, often in hair formulas.
how: Vitamin B5, used in energy metabolism and skin health.
avoid: Usually well tolerated.
about: Calcium pantothenate is a stable, common supplement form of pantothenic acid, also called vitamin B5. The body uses it to make coenzyme A, which is needed to turn food into energy and to build fats and hormones. It is often combined with other vitamins and ingredients in compounded hair and skin support capsules so several ingredients can be taken in one dose.
serious: Get medical or veterinary help right away for signs of an allergic reaction, such as hives, swelling of the face or trouble breathing, which are rare.
interactions: Serious interactions are not common with vitamin B5. Tell your prescriber about other vitamins or hair supplements so the same ingredients are not doubled up. Give your prescriber, or your pet's veterinarian, a full list of medicines, supplements and flea or tick products.
pregnancy: Normal dietary amounts of vitamin B5 are considered safe in pregnancy and breastfeeding, but ask your prescriber before taking a supplement or hair formula while pregnant or nursing.
petNotes: Pets usually get enough vitamin B5 from a complete diet, so supplements are given only when a veterinarian recommends them. Check with your veterinarian before giving a human hair or vitamin formula to a pet.
tips: Take it with food if it upsets your stomach.
Take it at about the same time each day so it becomes part of your routine.
Hair formulas usually take a few months of steady use before changes can be judged.
monitoring: Routine monitoring is usually not needed, but keep follow-up visits your prescriber or veterinarian schedules.
faqs: What is the difference between calcium pantothenate and pantothenic acid?
Calcium pantothenate is the calcium salt of pantothenic acid. It is more stable, which is why it is the form used in most supplements; in the body it provides vitamin B5.
Why is vitamin B5 in hair formulas?
Vitamin B5 plays a role in skin and hair cell metabolism, so it is often included in hair support blends. It is used as a supporting ingredient, and results vary from person to person.

name: Capsaicin
uses: Topical pain relief.
how: Depletes substance P from nerve endings, reducing pain signals over time.
avoid: Broken skin, eyes and mucous membranes; wash hands after use.
about: Capsaicin is the natural compound that makes chili peppers hot. Applied to the skin over time, it reduces substance P in local nerve endings, so pain signals weaken with regular use. Over-the-counter creams have been used for decades; compounded versions let a prescriber choose the strength and combine it with other ingredients, such as an anti-inflammatory, in one cream.
serious: Get medical help right away for severe burning, blistering or swelling of the skin, signs of an allergic reaction, or if it gets into the eyes and pain does not ease after rinsing.
interactions: Interactions are unlikely with topical capsaicin because little reaches the bloodstream. Avoid using heating pads or other heat-producing products on the same area. Give your prescriber a full list of medicines and supplements.
pregnancy: Little is known about capsaicin use in pregnancy and breastfeeding, so talk to your prescriber first, and keep it off the breast area if nursing.
tips: Apply it regularly as directed; relief often builds over the first one to two weeks.
Wash your hands with soap and water right after applying, unless your hands are the area being treated.
Do not apply heat, a heating pad or a tight bandage over the treated area, and avoid a hot shower right before or after.
Keep it away from eyes, nose, mouth and contact lenses.
monitoring: Routine monitoring is usually not needed, but keep follow-up visits your prescriber schedules.
faqs: How long does capsaicin cream take to work?
It often takes one to two weeks of regular use before pain relief is noticed. Skipping applications can slow results.
Does the burning feeling go away?
The warm or burning feeling is usually strongest in the first several days and tends to fade with continued use. Tell your prescriber if it stays severe.
What should I do if capsaicin gets in my eyes?
Rinse with plenty of cool water. Using a little vegetable oil on the skin before washing with soap can help remove it, and get medical care if pain continues.

name: Carprofen
uses: Arthritis and pain after surgery in dogs.
side: Stomach upset, liver and kidney effects.
how: A veterinary NSAID that reduces inflammation and pain.
avoid: Cats, and dogs with liver or kidney disease or taking steroids.
about: Carprofen is a nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug made for dogs and has been widely used in veterinary practice since the 1990s. It eases pain and swelling from arthritis and surgery. Compounded capsules may help when a dog needs a strength or form that is not commercially available, or has trouble with the usual chewable or tablet.
serious: Call your veterinarian right away for vomiting, black or bloody stools, loss of appetite, yellow gums, skin or eyes, increased thirst or urination, or unusual tiredness.
interactions: Do not combine carprofen with other NSAIDs, aspirin or steroids such as prednisone or dexamethasone, because this raises the risk of stomach ulcers. Use with diuretics or some heart medicines may affect the kidneys. Tell your veterinarian about every medicine, supplement and flea or tick product your pet gets.
petNotes: Carprofen is for dogs; cats are much more sensitive to NSAIDs and should not get it unless a veterinarian directs a specific plan. Liver problems have been reported, including in Labrador retrievers, so watch for appetite changes and keep pills out of reach to prevent overdose.
tips: Give it with food to help protect the stomach.
Allow a break between carprofen and any other anti-inflammatory as your veterinarian directs.
Store it out of reach, since dogs may eat a whole bottle of flavored medicine.
If you miss a dose, give it when you remember unless it is almost time for the next one; don't double up.
monitoring: Your veterinarian may check liver and kidney bloodwork before starting and periodically during long-term use.
faqs: Can I give my dog carprofen with gabapentin?
Yes, veterinarians often use them together, since they ease pain in different ways. Follow your veterinarian's directions for each one.
Is carprofen safe for cats?
Cats are especially sensitive to NSAIDs, and carprofen is not used in cats outside of specific veterinary direction. Never give a cat a dog's carprofen.
How long does carprofen take to work?
Many dogs show some improvement within a few hours to a few days. For arthritis, your veterinarian may judge results over a couple of weeks.

name: Cefpodoxime
uses: Skin and urinary infections in dogs.
how: A cephalosporin antibiotic that breaks down bacterial cell walls.
avoid: Pets with a cephalosporin allergy.
about: Cefpodoxime is an oral third-generation cephalosporin antibiotic. A veterinary tablet is approved for skin infections in dogs, and it is also used for urinary infections. Because it is usually given once a day, many owners find it convenient. A flavored suspension or chewable treat can help dogs that refuse tablets or need a size between tablet strengths.
serious: Call your veterinarian right away for hives, facial swelling, trouble breathing, collapse, severe vomiting or bloody diarrhea.
interactions: Antacids and stomach acid reducers may lower absorption of cefpodoxime. Probenecid can raise its levels. Tell your veterinarian about every medicine, supplement and flea or tick product your pet gets.
petNotes: Cefpodoxime is mainly used in dogs; use in cats is off-label and decided by the veterinarian. Giving it with food can ease stomach upset and may help absorption.
tips: Give it with food unless your veterinarian says otherwise.
Shake the suspension well and measure each dose with the syringe provided.
Finish the full course, even if your dog seems better.
If you miss a dose, give it when you remember unless it is almost time for the next one; don't double up.
monitoring: Your veterinarian may recheck the skin or urine, or run a culture, to make sure the infection has cleared.
faqs: How long does cefpodoxime take to work for a skin infection?
Many dogs start to improve within a few days, but skin infections often need several weeks of treatment. Your veterinarian decides when to stop.
Can my dog take cefpodoxime if allergic to penicillin?
Cefpodoxime is related to penicillin, and some pets allergic to one react to the other. Tell your veterinarian about any past drug reactions.

name: Ceftazidime
uses: Bacterial infections, including specialty topical preparations.
how: A cephalosporin antibiotic active against Pseudomonas.
avoid: People or pets with a cephalosporin allergy.
about: Ceftazidime is a third-generation cephalosporin antibiotic, normally given by injection in hospitals, that is valued for its activity against Pseudomonas and some other hard-to-treat bacteria. In compounding, it is used in specialty topical preparations, such as veterinary ear packs and transdermal gels, often combined with steroids or antifungals so one product treats several problems at once. These topical uses are off-label.
serious: Get medical or veterinary help right away for hives, facial swelling, trouble breathing, or severe pain, swelling or discharge where it was applied.
interactions: Topical ceftazidime has few interactions because little reaches the bloodstream. Do not use other ear cleaners or ear medicines during treatment unless directed. Give your prescriber, or your pet's veterinarian, a full list of medicines, supplements and flea or tick products.
pregnancy: Ceftazidime is generally considered low risk in pregnancy and breastfeeding, but talk to your prescriber before using any compounded antibiotic if you are pregnant or nursing.
petNotes: Ear packs are placed in the ear canal by the veterinarian and slowly release medicine for days; do not clean the ears or put other products in them unless told to. Do not use in ears with a ruptured eardrum unless your veterinarian approves.
tips: Follow the veterinarian's plan for when the ear pack will be rechecked or removed.
Wear gloves when applying a transdermal gel and wash your hands afterward.
Keep the treated area clean and stop your pet from scratching or rubbing it.
monitoring: Your prescriber or veterinarian will usually recheck the treated area, and may repeat an ear swab or culture, to confirm the infection has cleared.
faqs: Why is ceftazidime used in ear preparations?

It is active against Pseudomonas, a bacteria that commonly causes stubborn ear infections in dogs. Combining it with other ingredients lets a veterinarian treat bacteria, yeast and inflammation together.
How long does an ear pack stay in?
Ear packs are designed to stay in the ear and release medicine over several days. Your veterinarian will tell you when to return for a recheck.

name: Cephalexin
uses: Skin and other bacterial infections.
how: A cephalosporin antibiotic that breaks down bacterial cell walls.
avoid: People with a serious penicillin or cephalosporin allergy.
about: Cephalexin is a first-generation cephalosporin antibiotic that has been prescribed for people and pets since the 1970s. It is commonly used for skin, soft tissue, bone and urinary infections caused by susceptible bacteria. Compounded chewable treats or liquids can help pets that will not take capsules and patients who need a dose between commercial strengths.
serious: Get medical or veterinary help right away for hives, swelling of the face or throat, trouble breathing, a blistering or peeling rash, or severe, watery or bloody diarrhea.
interactions: Probenecid can raise cephalexin levels, and metformin levels may rise when the two are used together. Give your prescriber, or your pet's veterinarian, a full list of medicines, supplements and flea or tick products.
pregnancy: Cephalexin is often used in pregnancy and breastfeeding when an antibiotic is needed, but your prescriber decides whether it is right for you.
petNotes: Cephalexin is used in both dogs and cats, and stomach upset is the most common problem; giving it with a small meal often helps. Flavored chewables and liquids make it easier to finish a full course.
tips: It can be taken with or without food; taking it with food may ease stomach upset.
Shake liquids well and keep them as directed on the label.
Finish the full course even if symptoms improve.
If you miss a dose, take it when you remember unless it is almost time for the next one; don't double up.
monitoring: Routine monitoring is usually not needed, but keep follow-up visits your prescriber or veterinarian schedules, especially for long courses.
faqs: Can I take cephalexin if I am allergic to penicillin?
Some people allergic to penicillin can take cephalexin, but those with a serious reaction usually should not. Your prescriber decides based on your allergy history.
Can I drink alcohol while taking cephalexin?
Alcohol is not known to interact directly with cephalexin, but it can worsen stomach upset and slow recovery. Ask your prescriber if you are unsure.
How long does cephalexin take to work?
Many infections start to improve within a few days. Keep taking it for the full time prescribed.

name: Cetirizine
uses: Allergy and itch relief.
how: An antihistamine that blocks H1 receptors.
avoid: People or pets with kidney or liver disease (lower dose).
about: Cetirizine is a second-generation antihistamine that has been sold since the 1990s and is now available over the counter. It blocks histamine to ease sneezing, runny nose, itchy eyes, hives and itching, and causes less drowsiness than older antihistamines for most people. Veterinarians also use it off-label for itchy skin in dogs and cats. Compounded capsules or flavored liquids allow doses for small pets or people who cannot swallow tablets.
conditions: Allergic itching in dogs and cats
serious: Get medical or veterinary help right away for signs of an allergic reaction, a fast or irregular heartbeat, trouble urinating, or unusual agitation or confusion.
interactions: Alcohol, sleep aids, sedatives and opioid pain medicines can add to drowsiness. Avoid using other antihistamines at the same time unless directed. Give your prescriber, or your pet's veterinarian, a full list of medicines, supplements and flea or tick products.
pregnancy: Cetirizine is commonly used in pregnancy and passes into breast milk in small amounts, so talk to your prescriber before using it if you are pregnant or breastfeeding.
petNotes: Never give a pet a product that also contains a decongestant, such as Zyrtec-D, because pseudoephedrine can be very dangerous for dogs and cats. It is generally well tolerated in dogs and cats, and some pets may be mildly sleepy.
tips: It can be taken with or without food.
If it makes you sleepy, taking it in the evening may help.
Shake the suspension well before measuring each dose.
Avoid driving until you know how it affects you.
monitoring: Routine monitoring is usually not needed, but keep follow-up visits your prescriber or veterinarian schedules.
faqs: Is cetirizine safe for dogs and cats?
Veterinarians commonly use it off-label in dogs and cats for itchy skin. Use only a product and dose your veterinarian recommends, and never one that contains a decongestant.
What is the difference between cetirizine and levocetirizine?
Levocetirizine is the active half of the cetirizine molecule. They work the same way; your prescriber chooses which one fits you.
How fast does cetirizine work?
It often starts working within an hour. For ongoing allergies, your prescriber may suggest steady daily use.

name: Chlorambucil
uses: Some cancers and immune diseases in cats and dogs, especially small-cell lymphoma in cats.
side: Bone marrow suppression; hazardous drug requiring careful handling.
how: Damages DNA in rapidly dividing cells, such as cancer and immune cells.
avoid: Pregnancy. Hazardous drug: wear gloves and never split or crush.
about: Chlorambucil is an oral chemotherapy drug that has been used since the 1950s. In veterinary medicine it is used off-label, often with prednisolone, for small-cell lymphoma in cats, some leukemias and certain immune diseases. Commercial tablets come in a single strength that is hard to fit small pets, so compounded capsules or tablets let the veterinarian order an exact dose without splitting or crushing a hazardous drug.
conditions: Chronic lymphocytic leukemia in dogs and cats
Immune-mediated diseases in dogs and cats
serious: Call your veterinarian right away for fever, lethargy, pale gums, unusual bruising or bleeding, severe vomiting or diarrhea, or not eating.
interactions: Other drugs that suppress the bone marrow or immune system add to the risk of infection and low blood counts. Do not give vaccines or new medicines without asking your veterinarian. Tell your veterinarian about every medicine, supplement and flea or tick product your pet gets.
petNotes: Cats generally handle chlorambucil well, and it is often paired with prednisolone for small-cell lymphoma. Pregnant people and children should not handle it, and pet waste should be handled with gloves for a few days after each dose.
tips: Wear disposable gloves when giving it and wash your hands afterward.
Give it whole; never split, crush or open the capsules.
Pick up stool and clean the litter box with gloves, and keep children away from pet waste after dosing.
Store it in its original labeled container, away from food, children and other pets.
monitoring: Your veterinarian will check complete blood counts regularly to watch for bone marrow suppression.
faqs: Is chlorambucil safe to handle at home?
It is a hazardous drug, so wear gloves, don't split or crush it, and keep it away from children and anyone who is pregnant. Following these steps lowers exposure.
How do cats do on chlorambucil?
Many cats with small-cell lymphoma tolerate it well, often for long periods, with regular blood checks. Your veterinarian decides the plan and watches for side effects.

name: Chloramphenicol
uses: Resistant bacterial infections.
side: Bone marrow effects; hazardous for people handling it.
how: Stops bacteria from making proteins.
avoid: Pregnancy and people handling it with bare hands; can cause serious blood disorders in people.
about: Chloramphenicol is a broad-spectrum antibiotic first used in the late 1940s. Because it can cause rare but serious blood disorders in people, its use in human medicine is now limited, and it is kept mostly for resistant infections, especially in veterinary practice. Commercial oral products for animals are hard to find, so it is often compounded into capsules for pets with infections that do not respond to other antibiotics.
serious: Get medical or veterinary help right away for unusual tiredness, pale skin or gums, fever, sore throat, unusual bruising or bleeding, or signs of an allergic reaction.
interactions: Chloramphenicol can raise levels of phenobarbital, phenytoin, warfarin and some other drugs, and should not be combined with other medicines that suppress the bone marrow. Give your prescriber, or your pet's veterinarian, a full list of medicines, supplements and flea or tick products.
pregnancy: Chloramphenicol is not used in pregnancy or breastfeeding, and anyone pregnant should not handle it.
petNotes: Cats are more sensitive to its effects on the bone marrow than dogs, so treatment is usually kept short. Wear gloves when giving it, because rare blood disorders have occurred in people exposed to the drug.
tips: Always wear gloves when handling capsules and wash your hands afterward.
Give it as directed, usually with a small amount of food if it upsets the stomach.
Finish the full course your prescriber or veterinarian ordered.
Keep it away from children and anyone who is pregnant.
monitoring: Your prescriber or veterinarian may check complete blood counts during treatment, especially for longer courses.
faqs: Why do I need gloves to give chloramphenicol to my pet?
In rare cases, people exposed to even small amounts have developed serious blood disorders. Gloves and hand washing reduce that risk.
Why is chloramphenicol used if it has risks?
It works against some bacteria that resist other antibiotics. Your prescriber or veterinarian weighs the risks when other options are not suitable.

name: Chlorpheniramine
uses: Allergy and itch relief; commonly used for cats.
how: A sedating antihistamine that blocks H1 receptors.
avoid: People or pets with glaucoma, urinary retention or heart disease.
about: Chlorpheniramine is a first-generation antihistamine that has been available for decades in over-the-counter allergy and cold products. It relieves sneezing, runny nose, itching and hives, and can cause drowsiness. Veterinarians use it off-label, especially in cats, for itchy skin and allergies. Compounding allows small, flavored doses for cats and other pets, slow-release capsules, or a transdermal gel for pets that are hard to pill.
serious: Get medical or veterinary help right away for a fast or irregular heartbeat, trouble urinating, severe confusion or agitation, seizures, or signs of an allergic reaction.
interactions: Alcohol, sleep aids, sedatives, opioid pain medicines and other antihistamines can add to drowsiness. MAO inhibitors and some antidepressants can increase side effects. Give your prescriber, or your pet's veterinarian, a full list of medicines, supplements and flea or tick products.
pregnancy: Chlorpheniramine has been used in pregnancy, but it may pass into breast milk and cause drowsiness in a nursing baby, so ask your prescriber before using it.
petNotes: Cats often accept it best as a small flavored treat or liquid, since the tablets taste bitter. Never give pets combination cold products, which may contain decongestants or acetaminophen that are dangerous for them.
tips: It can be given with or without food; food may ease stomach upset.
Wear gloves when applying transdermal gel to a pet's ear and wash your hands afterward.
Swallow slow-release capsules whole without opening or chewing them.
Avoid driving or other risky tasks until you know how drowsy it makes you.
monitoring: Routine monitoring is usually not needed, but keep follow-up visits your prescriber or veterinarian schedules.
faqs: Is chlorpheniramine safe for cats?
It is commonly used off-label in cats for itching and allergies. Use only the product and amount your veterinarian prescribes.
Does chlorpheniramine make you sleepy?
Yes, drowsiness is common because it is an older antihistamine. Some people and pets become sleepy while a few become restless.

name: Cholecalciferol (vitamin D3)
uses: Vitamin D supplement.
how: Vitamin D3, which the body converts to active vitamin D for calcium balance.
avoid: Too much can cause high calcium; accidental ingestion is dangerous for dogs.
about: Cholecalciferol is vitamin D3, the form the skin makes in sunlight. The liver and kidneys convert it to active vitamin D, which helps the body absorb calcium and keep bones strong. It is one of the most widely used supplements. Compounded liquids or capsules allow a prescriber to choose an exact amount for children, adults with absorption problems or pets with a diagnosed need.
conditions: Low calcium from low vitamin D
serious: Get medical or veterinary help right away for signs of too much vitamin D, such as vomiting, loss of appetite, increased thirst and urination, constipation, weakness or confusion. If a dog or cat eats vitamin D supplements or rodent bait, call a veterinarian or animal poison control right away.
interactions: Thiazide diuretics and calcium supplements can raise calcium levels further, and high calcium can increase the effects of digoxin. Some seizure medicines, steroids and cholestyramine can lower vitamin D levels. Give your prescriber, or your pet's veterinarian, a full list of medicines, supplements and flea or tick products.
pregnancy: Vitamin D is part of most prenatal vitamins, but ask your prescriber before taking extra if you are pregnant or breastfeeding.
petNotes: Dogs and cats get vitamin D from their food, and supplements are given only when a veterinarian finds a need. Pets are very sensitive to vitamin D overdose, so store supplements and rodent poisons well out of reach.
tips: Take it with a meal that contains some fat to help absorption.
Shake the suspension well before each dose.
Count all sources, including multivitamins, so you do not take more than prescribed.
Store it out of reach of children and pets.
monitoring: Your prescriber or veterinarian may check vitamin D and calcium levels to guide the dose.
faqs: What is the difference between vitamin D3 and vitamin D2?
Vitamin D3 (cholecalciferol) is the form made in skin, and D2 (ergocalciferol) comes from plants and fungi. Both raise vitamin D levels; your prescriber chooses which to use.
Why is vitamin D dangerous for dogs?
Dogs can get very high calcium levels from eating vitamin D supplements or certain rodent baits, which can damage the kidneys. Treat any accidental ingestion as an emergency.
How long does it take to raise vitamin D levels?
It usually takes weeks to a few months of steady use. Your prescriber may recheck a blood level after that time.

name: Cholestyramine
uses: Bile acid binder; in barrier ointments for diaper and perianal skin irritation.
how: Binds bile acids, which can irritate skin in diaper and perianal areas.
avoid: Open wounds.
about: Cholestyramine is a resin that binds bile acids. It has long been taken by mouth to lower cholesterol and treat itching from bile buildup. Compounded into a barrier ointment, it is used off-label to protect skin in the diaper and perianal area, where bile acids in loose or frequent stools can cause painful irritation. It is often combined with soothing, antifungal or antibacterial ingredients.
serious: Get medical help right away for spreading redness, open sores, blistering, fever, or signs of an allergic reaction such as hives or swelling.
interactions: Interactions are unlikely when the ointment is used on the skin. Ask before applying other creams or powders to the same area. Give your prescriber a full list of medicines and supplements.
pregnancy: Topical cholestyramine is not expected to be absorbed into the body, but talk to your prescriber before using it if you are pregnant or breastfeeding.
tips: Gently clean and pat the skin dry before each application.
Apply a thick layer at each diaper change or after each bowel movement as directed.
You do not need to scrub off all of the old ointment; gently remove soiled areas and reapply.
Wash your hands before and after applying.
monitoring: Routine monitoring is usually not needed, but keep follow-up visits your prescriber schedules, and let them know if the rash is not improving.
faqs: Why is cholestyramine used for diaper rash?
Bile acids in frequent or loose stools can irritate and break down skin. Cholestyramine binds these acids, and the ointment base adds a protective barrier.
Is this the same as cholestyramine powder taken by mouth?
It is the same ingredient, but here it is mixed into an ointment for the skin and is not meant to be swallowed.

name: Cinacalcet
uses: High parathyroid hormone and high calcium.
how: Makes the parathyroid gland more sensitive to calcium, lowering parathyroid hormone.
avoid: People or pets with low calcium or seizures.
about: Cinacalcet is a calcimimetic, a medicine that makes the calcium-sensing receptors in the parathyroid glands more sensitive. This lowers parathyroid hormone and blood calcium. It has been used in people since the 2000s for parathyroid problems related to kidney disease and parathyroid tumors. A compounded flavored suspension can help people who cannot swallow tablets and pets that need small doses; veterinary use is off-label.
serious: Get medical or veterinary help right away for signs of low calcium, such as muscle cramps, twitching, numbness or tingling around the mouth, or seizures.
interactions: Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors such as ketoconazole can raise cinacalcet levels, and it can raise levels of some antidepressants and heart medicines. Other medicines that lower calcium add to the risk of low calcium. Give your prescriber, or your pet's veterinarian, a full list of medicines, supplements and flea or tick products.
pregnancy: There is limited information on cinacalcet in pregnancy and breastfeeding, so talk to your prescriber before using it.
petNotes: Use in dogs and cats is off-label and less common, and dosing is set by the veterinarian with close calcium checks. Give it with food to help absorption and reduce vomiting.
tips: Take or give it with food or shortly after a meal.
Shake the suspension well before measuring each dose.
Take it at the same time each day.
If you miss a dose, take it when you remember unless it is almost time for the next one; don't double up.
monitoring: Your prescriber or veterinarian will check blood calcium and parathyroid hormone levels regularly, especially after starting or changing the dose.
faqs: Why should cinacalcet be taken with food?
Food increases how much is absorbed and can reduce nausea. Taking it the same way each day keeps levels steady.
What are signs of low calcium on cinacalcet?
Watch for tingling around the mouth, muscle cramps or twitching. Contact your prescriber or veterinarian if these occur.

name: Ciprofloxacin
uses: Bacterial infections.
side: Stomach upset, tendon problems in people.
how: A fluoroquinolone that blocks bacterial DNA copying.
avoid: Children, people over 60 on steroids (tendon risk), and people with myasthenia gravis.
about: Ciprofloxacin is a fluoroquinolone antibiotic that has been used since the late 1980s for many bacterial infections, including urinary, respiratory, bone and gastrointestinal infections. Because of risks such as tendon problems, it is usually reserved for infections where other antibiotics are not suitable. Veterinarians sometimes use it off-label. Compounded capsules, powders and liquids help when tablets are not practical.
serious: Get medical or veterinary help right away for tendon pain, swelling or a pop near a tendon; numbness, tingling or burning in the hands or feet; severe diarrhea; confusion, seizures or mood changes; a fast heartbeat; or signs of an allergic reaction.
interactions: Antacids, calcium, iron, zinc and magnesium products can block absorption, so take ciprofloxacin a few hours before or after them. It can raise levels of tizanidine, theophylline and warfarin, and steroids increase the tendon risk. Give your prescriber, or your pet's veterinarian, a full list of medicines, supplements and flea or tick products.
pregnancy: Ciprofloxacin is usually avoided in pregnancy and breastfeeding unless your prescriber decides the benefit outweighs the risk.
petNotes: Use in pets is off-label; veterinarians more often choose a veterinary fluoroquinolone. Fluoroquinolones can affect growing cartilage in young dogs, and some have caused vision problems in cats, so your veterinarian chooses carefully.
tips: Drink plenty of fluids while taking it.
Separate it from dairy, calcium-fortified juice, antacids and mineral supplements by a few hours.
Limit caffeine, since ciprofloxacin can increase its effects.
Avoid strong sun or tanning beds, since it can make skin burn more easily.
monitoring: Routine lab monitoring is usually not needed for short courses, but your prescriber may check kidney function or blood sugar in some patients.
faqs: Can I take ciprofloxacin with milk?
Dairy and calcium-fortified foods can reduce absorption if taken alone with the dose. It can be taken with a full meal, but avoid taking it with only milk or yogurt.
Why does ciprofloxacin have a tendon warning?
Fluoroquinolones can cause tendon inflammation or rupture, especially in older adults and people taking steroids. Stop and call your prescriber if you have tendon pain.
Is ciprofloxacin safe for dogs?
Veterinarians sometimes use it off-label in adult dogs. It is generally avoided in growing puppies.

name: Cisapride
uses: Constipation and megacolon in cats and slow stomach emptying in pets; available only by compounding.
how: Stimulates serotonin (5-HT4) receptors in the gut to strengthen movement of the stomach and colon.
avoid: Pets with a bowel blockage or heart rhythm problems, or taking antifungals like ketoconazole. No longer sold commercially, so it is available only by compounding.
about: Cisapride is a prokinetic medicine that helps the stomach and intestines move food along. It was withdrawn from the human market in 2000 because of heart rhythm problems in people, but veterinarians still use it, and it is now available only through compounding. It is especially known for helping cats with chronic constipation and megacolon.
conditions: Delayed stomach emptying in dogs and cats
serious: Call your veterinarian right away for severe vomiting, belly pain or swelling, no stool for several days, collapse, fainting or a very fast or irregular heartbeat.
interactions: Azole antifungals such as ketoconazole and itraconazole, erythromycin and clarithromycin can raise cisapride levels and increase heart rhythm risk. Medicines that slow the gut, such as some antihistamines and opioid pain medicines, may work against it. Tell your veterinarian about every medicine, supplement and flea or tick product your pet gets.
petNotes: It is used mainly in cats for constipation and megacolon, often together with stool softeners or diet changes. It is usually given before meals; flavored liquids, treats or transdermal gel can help cats that are hard to pill.
tips: Give it before meals, as your veterinarian directs.
Shake liquid forms well before each dose.
Wear gloves when applying transdermal gel to the ear and wash your hands afterward.
Make sure your cat has plenty of water, and watch the litter box for changes.
monitoring: Your veterinarian will follow bowel habits and may recheck X-rays or bloodwork depending on the underlying condition.
faqs: Why is cisapride available only by compounding?
It was removed from the human market because of heart rhythm problems in people. Veterinarians still prescribe it, so compounding pharmacies prepare it from the bulk ingredient.
How long does cisapride take to work in cats?
Some cats have more regular stools within days, but it can take longer to see the full effect. Your veterinarian may adjust the plan based on how your cat does.

name: Clindamycin
uses: Skin, dental and bone infections; acne creams; toxoplasmosis in cats.
how: Stops bacteria from making proteins; especially active against anaerobes and toxoplasma.
avoid: Rabbits, guinea pigs and hamsters. People with a history of C. diff colitis.
about: Clindamycin is a lincosamide antibiotic used since the 1970s. It is especially active against anaerobic bacteria and some staph and strep, which makes it useful for dental, bone and skin infections. Veterinarians also use it for toxoplasmosis in cats. Applied to the skin, it calms acne. Compounded flavored liquids help hide its very bitter taste for pets, and topical gels can be combined with other acne ingredients.
serious: Get medical or veterinary help right away for severe, watery or bloody diarrhea, even weeks after stopping, as well as a blistering rash, yellow skin or eyes, or signs of an allergic reaction.
interactions: Erythromycin can work against clindamycin, and it may increase the effects of some muscle relaxants used in surgery. Strong CYP3A4 drugs can change its levels. Give your prescriber, or your pet's veterinarian, a full list of medicines, supplements and flea or tick products.
pregnancy: Clindamycin is generally considered acceptable in pregnancy when needed, and small amounts pass into breast milk, so talk to your prescriber about your situation.
petNotes: Never give clindamycin to rabbits, guinea pigs, hamsters, chinchillas or horses, because it can cause fatal gut problems. Follow each dose with food or water in cats, since capsules can irritate the esophagus.
tips: Take capsules with a full glass of water and stay upright for a while afterward.
Shake the suspension well; a flavored liquid helps mask its bitter taste.
For acne gel, apply a thin layer to clean, dry skin and avoid eyes and lips.
Finish the full course of oral antibiotics even if symptoms improve.
monitoring: Routine monitoring is usually not needed, but call your prescriber or veterinarian about any ongoing diarrhea.
faqs: Why does clindamycin taste so bad?
Clindamycin is very bitter, which is why pets often drool or refuse it. Flavored compounded liquids are made to help with this.
Can clindamycin cause diarrhea?
Yes. Mild diarrhea is common, but severe or bloody diarrhea can be a sign of C. diff infection and needs prompt medical attention.
Is clindamycin safe for cats?
Veterinarians commonly prescribe it for cats for dental infections and toxoplasmosis. Give it with food or a little water to protect the esophagus.

name: Clobetasol
uses: Very potent steroid for stubborn skin conditions such as lichen sclerosus and psoriasis.
side: Skin thinning; use only as directed.
how: A very potent steroid for short-term use on stubborn inflammation.
avoid: Use on the face, groin or large areas only when directed; not for long-term use.
about: Clobetasol propionate is one of the strongest topical steroids available and has been prescribed since the 1980s. It calms stubborn redness, itching and thickened skin when milder steroids are not enough. It is usually used for short periods or on a schedule your prescriber sets. Compounded creams and vaginal preparations can combine it with other ingredients, such as moisturizers or hormones, for conditions like lichen sclerosus.
serious: Get medical help right away for signs of skin infection, severe burning or irritation, or signs of too much steroid absorbed into the body, such as unusual tiredness, weight change, blurred vision or high blood sugar.
interactions: Avoid using other steroid creams on the same area unless directed. Large-area use is of more concern in people taking oral steroids or certain antifungal and HIV medicines. Give your prescriber a full list of medicines and supplements.
pregnancy: Use in pregnancy and breastfeeding should be limited to small areas for short periods as your prescriber directs, and do not apply to the breast or nipple if nursing.
tips: Apply a thin layer only to affected skin and rub it in gently.
Do not cover it with a bandage or tight clothing unless your prescriber tells you to.
Wash your hands after applying unless you are treating your hands.
Follow the schedule given; many plans taper down to less frequent use.
monitoring: Your prescriber will check your skin at follow-up visits for improvement and for thinning or other side effects.
faqs: How long can I use clobetasol?
It is usually used for short periods, often a few weeks at a time, unless your prescriber sets a longer maintenance plan, such as for lichen sclerosus.
Can clobetasol be used on the face?
It is generally avoided on the face because the skin is thin. Use it there only if your prescriber specifically directs you to.
Why is clobetasol used for lichen sclerosus?
Strong steroids calm the inflammation and itching that cause skin changes in lichen sclerosus. Your prescriber sets a schedule and follows you over time.

name: Clomiphene
uses: Ovulation induction in women and, off-label, support of natural testosterone production in men.
side: Hot flashes, mood changes, visual disturbances, headache.
how: Blocks estrogen's signal in the brain, which prompts the pituitary gland to release more of the hormones that drive ovulation and testosterone production.
avoid: People with liver disease, ovarian cysts, unexplained uterine bleeding or vision problems, and those who are pregnant.
about: Clomiphene citrate is a selective estrogen receptor modulator that has been used since the 1960s to help women ovulate. By blocking estrogen feedback in the brain, it raises the hormones that trigger ovulation and, in men, testosterone production. Its use in men is off-label. Compounded capsules allow strengths that fit the dose your prescriber orders.
serious: Get medical help right away for blurred vision, spots or flashes, severe pelvic or belly pain, sudden weight gain or swelling, shortness of breath, or signs of a blood clot such as leg pain or swelling.
interactions: Clomiphene is generally not combined with estrogen or testosterone therapy without your prescriber's plan. Give your prescriber a full list of medicines and supplements.
pregnancy: Clomiphene should not be taken once you are pregnant; stop and contact your prescriber if you think you may be pregnant, and it is not used while breastfeeding.
tips: Take it at the same time each day on the days your prescriber specifies.
Write down the days you start and stop it, along with any symptoms.
Avoid driving or other risky tasks if you notice vision changes, and report them right away.
If you miss a dose, take it when you remember unless it is almost time for the next one; don't double up.
monitoring: Your prescriber may use ultrasound, hormone blood tests or ovulation tracking for fertility treatment, or check testosterone and estrogen levels for men.
faqs: How long does clomiphene take to work?
For fertility, ovulation usually occurs about a week after finishing a cycle of tablets. For men, testosterone levels are often rechecked after several weeks.
Does clomiphene raise the chance of twins?
Yes, it can increase the chance of multiple pregnancy. Your prescriber can explain the risks for your situation.
Why do men take clomiphene?
It is used off-label to prompt the body to make more of its own testosterone. Your prescriber decides if it fits your situation.

name: Clomipramine
uses: Obsessive-compulsive disorder in people; separation anxiety and compulsive behaviors in dogs and cats.
how: A tricyclic that increases serotonin and norepinephrine.
avoid: People or pets with heart rhythm problems, glaucoma or seizures, and anyone on MAO inhibitors.
about: Clomipramine is a tricyclic antidepressant that strongly affects serotonin. It has been used for decades for obsessive-compulsive disorder in people, and a veterinary product is approved for separation anxiety in dogs. Veterinarians also use it off-label for compulsive behaviors and some cases of urine marking in cats. Compounded transdermal gel or paste can help with pets that are difficult to pill.
conditions: Urine marking and overgrooming in cats
serious: Get medical or veterinary help right away for a fast or irregular heartbeat, fainting, seizures, severe agitation, high fever or stiff muscles, or in people, new or worsening depression or thoughts of self-harm.
interactions: Never combine clomipramine with MAO inhibitors, including selegiline or amitraz flea and tick products in pets. Other serotonin medicines, such as SSRIs and trazodone, and some heart rhythm medicines raise the risk of serious reactions. Give your prescriber, or your pet's veterinarian, a full list of medicines, supplements and flea or tick products.
pregnancy: Clomipramine may affect a newborn when used late in pregnancy and passes into breast milk, so talk to your prescriber before using it.
petNotes: Avoid flea and tick collars or dips containing amitraz while your pet takes clomipramine. It is usually used alongside a behavior plan, and cats may be more sensitive to sedation.
tips: Give it at the same time each day; it can be given with food to reduce stomach upset.
Wear gloves when applying transdermal gel or paste and wash your hands afterward.
Do not stop it suddenly; your prescriber or veterinarian will taper it.
Expect several weeks before the full effect is seen.
monitoring: Your prescriber or veterinarian may check heart rhythm or liver values, especially in older patients or with long-term use.
faqs: How long does clomipramine take to work for dog anxiety?
Some changes may show in the first week or two, but full effects often take several weeks. It is usually combined with behavior training.
Can clomipramine be given with flea and tick products?
Avoid products containing amitraz, which can interact. Check with your veterinarian before using any flea or tick product.

name: Clonidine
uses: Blood pressure, ADHD and sleep in people; anxiety in dogs.
side: Drowsiness, dry mouth, low blood pressure.
how: Stimulates alpha-2 receptors in the brain to reduce stress signals and lower blood pressure.
avoid: People or pets with slow heart rate or low blood pressure. Do not stop suddenly.
about: Clonidine is a central alpha-2 agonist first used in the 1960s to lower blood pressure. It calms certain nerve signals in the brain, and today it is also prescribed for ADHD and, off-label, for sleep and anxiety. Veterinarians use it off-label for situational anxiety in dogs. Compounded capsules allow small or specific doses for children, older adults and pets.
serious: Get medical or veterinary help right away for a very slow heartbeat, fainting, severe dizziness, trouble breathing, or extreme sleepiness. Stopping suddenly can cause a dangerous rise in blood pressure.
interactions: Alcohol, sedatives and opioid pain medicines add to drowsiness. Beta-blockers and other heart rate-lowering medicines can slow the heart further, and some antidepressants can reduce its effect. Give your prescriber, or your pet's veterinarian, a full list of medicines, supplements and flea or tick products.
pregnancy: Clonidine passes into breast milk, and its use in pregnancy should be decided with your prescriber.
petNotes: In dogs it is used off-label, often before stressful events such as storms or vet visits. Keep it well out of reach, since dogs that eat human clonidine tablets can become dangerously sleepy with a slow heart rate.
tips: Take it at the same times each day.
Stand up slowly to avoid dizziness.
Do not stop it suddenly; your prescriber or veterinarian will taper it.
Drink fluids and use sugar-free gum or candy for dry mouth, but never give xylitol products to pets.
monitoring: Your prescriber or veterinarian may check blood pressure and heart rate periodically.
faqs: Why can't clonidine be stopped suddenly?
Stopping suddenly can cause a rebound rise in blood pressure, nervousness and headache. Your prescriber will reduce it gradually.
Is clonidine used for anxiety in dogs?
Yes, veterinarians use it off-label for situational anxiety, sometimes with other behavior medicines. Your veterinarian decides when and how to give it.
Does clonidine make you sleepy?
Drowsiness is common, especially at first. Avoid driving until you know how it affects you.

name: Clopidogrel
uses: Prevents blood clots in people and in cats with heart disease.
how: Keeps platelets from sticking together, reducing the risk of clots.
avoid: People or pets with active bleeding, bleeding disorders or upcoming surgery.
about: Clopidogrel is an antiplatelet medicine that has been widely prescribed since the late 1990s to help prevent heart attacks and strokes in people. Veterinarians use it off-label, especially in cats with heart disease, to lower the risk of dangerous blood clots. The tablets taste very bitter, so compounded flavored liquids, chews, capsules and gels can make it easier to give to cats and small dogs.
conditions: Clot prevention in cats with heart disease
serious: Get medical or veterinary help right away for black or bloody stools, vomiting blood, blood in urine, unusual bruising, a sudden severe headache, or in cats, sudden pain or weakness in the back legs.
interactions: Aspirin, NSAIDs, blood thinners and some antidepressants raise the risk of bleeding. Omeprazole and esomeprazole may reduce how well clopidogrel works. Give your prescriber, or your pet's veterinarian, a full list of medicines, supplements and flea or tick products.
pregnancy: There is limited information on clopidogrel in pregnancy and breastfeeding, so talk to your prescriber before using it.
petNotes: Cats often foam or drool from the bitter taste of the tablets, which is why compounded flavored forms or capsules are used. Tell your veterinarian before any surgery or dental work.
tips: Give it at the same time each day, with or without food.
Do not stop it without talking to your prescriber or veterinarian, since clot risk can rise.
Tell dentists and surgeons that you or your pet take clopidogrel.
If you miss a dose, take it when you remember unless it is almost time for the next one; don't double up.
monitoring: Your prescriber or veterinarian will follow the underlying heart or blood vessel condition and may check blood counts if bleeding is a concern.
faqs: Why do cats with heart disease take clopidogrel?
Some cats with heart disease are at risk for blood clots that can block blood flow to the legs. Veterinarians use clopidogrel off-label to help lower that risk.
Can I take clopidogrel with ibuprofen?
Combining them increases the risk of bleeding. Ask your prescriber which pain reliever is safest for you.
Should I stop clopidogrel before surgery?
Only your prescriber can decide. Tell your surgeon or dentist you take it so they can plan with your prescriber.

name: Coenzyme Q10
uses: Heart and energy support supplement.
how: A compound cells use to make energy, with antioxidant effects.
avoid: People taking warfarin.
about: Coenzyme Q10 is a natural compound found in nearly every cell, where it helps make energy in the mitochondria and acts as an antioxidant. The body makes less of it with age, and some medicines, such as statins, can lower levels. It is a popular supplement for heart and energy support in people and is sometimes recommended by veterinarians for pets with heart disease.
serious: Get medical or veterinary help right away for signs of an allergic reaction, such as hives, swelling or trouble breathing, or unusual bleeding in someone taking a blood thinner.
interactions: Coenzyme Q10 may reduce the effect of warfarin and may lower blood pressure and blood sugar slightly when combined with medicines for those conditions. Give your prescriber, or your pet's veterinarian, a full list of medicines, supplements and flea or tick products.
pregnancy: There is not enough information on coenzyme Q10 supplements in pregnancy and breastfeeding, so ask your prescriber before using it.
petNotes: Veterinarians sometimes add it as a supplement for dogs and cats with heart disease. Giving it with a meal helps absorption, and it is generally well tolerated.
tips: Take it with a meal that contains some fat to improve absorption.
If it upsets your stomach, split the daily amount between meals as directed.
Taking it earlier in the day may help if it affects your sleep.
monitoring: Routine monitoring is usually not needed, but if you take warfarin your prescriber may check your INR more often.
faqs: Should I take CoQ10 if I take a statin?
Some people take it because statins can lower CoQ10 levels. Talk to your prescriber about whether it makes sense for you.
What is the difference between ubiquinone and ubiquinol?
They are two forms of coenzyme Q10, and the body converts one into the other. Your prescriber can tell you which form was ordered.

name: Collagen
uses: Skin, hair and joint support supplement.
how: Protein building blocks for skin, hair and joints.
avoid: People with allergies to the source (fish, beef or other).
about: Collagen is the main structural protein in skin, hair, nails, tendons and joints. Collagen supplements are usually hydrolyzed into small peptides that are easier to absorb and come from sources such as cows, pigs or fish. It is commonly added to compounded hair and skin support capsules alongside vitamins so several supportive ingredients can be taken together.
serious: Get medical help right away for signs of an allergic reaction, such as hives, swelling of the face or throat, or trouble breathing.
interactions: Collagen has no well-known serious drug interactions. Tell your prescriber about other supplements so ingredients are not doubled up. Give your prescriber a full list of medicines and supplements.
pregnancy: Collagen is a food protein, but there is little research on supplements in pregnancy and breastfeeding, so ask your prescriber before using it.
tips: Take it at the same time each day so it becomes routine.
Take it with food if it upsets your stomach.
Tell your prescriber or pharmacist about fish, beef or pork allergies or dietary restrictions so the source can be checked.
Skin and hair changes, if any, usually take a few months to judge.
monitoring: Routine monitoring is usually not needed, but keep follow-up visits your prescriber schedules.
faqs: Where does collagen come from?
Collagen supplements usually come from cows, pigs, chicken or fish. If you have an allergy or dietary restriction, ask about the source.
How long does collagen take to work for hair or skin?
Any changes usually take a few months of steady use, and results vary. Your prescriber can help you decide how long to try it.

name: Combination hormone preparations
uses: Two or more hormones, such as estriol, estradiol, estrone, progesterone, testosterone, DHEA and pregnenolone, combined in one cream, troche, capsule or vaginal preparation, in the amounts and ratio your prescriber orders.
side: Depends on the hormones included. May include breast tenderness, spotting, bloating, acne, hair growth or irritation where applied.
how: Each hormone works as it does on its own. Combining them lets you use a single preparation for your prescribed doses instead of several separate ones.
avoid: People with a history of hormone-sensitive cancer, blood clots, stroke, liver disease or unexplained vaginal bleeding. Your prescriber monitors your hormone levels and symptoms.
about: Combination hormone preparations put two or more hormones, such as estrogens, progesterone, testosterone or DHEA, into one product in the ratio your prescriber orders. Commercial products usually contain fixed amounts of one or two hormones, so compounding lets a prescriber tailor the mix and choose a form such as a cream, troche or capsule. These preparations are not FDA-approved, and your prescriber decides which hormones and amounts are right for you.
conditions: Hormone balance in women and men
serious: Get medical help right away for chest pain, shortness of breath, leg pain or swelling, sudden severe headache, vision or speech changes, weakness on one side, unusual vaginal bleeding, or a new breast lump.
interactions: Some seizure medicines, rifampin and St. John's wort can lower hormone levels, and hormones can affect thyroid medicine and blood thinner needs. Avoid using other hormone products at the same time unless your prescriber plans it. Give your prescriber a full list of medicines and supplements.
pregnancy: These preparations are not used during pregnancy or breastfeeding; tell your prescriber if you are pregnant or could become pregnant.
tips: Use it at the same time each day, and rotate application sites for creams and gels.
Let creams and gels dry and wash your hands; keep treated skin away from children, partners and pets.
Let troches dissolve fully between the cheek and gum without chewing or swallowing them whole.
Keep a symptom diary to share with your prescriber at follow-up visits.
monitoring: Your prescriber will usually check hormone levels and symptoms after starting or changing the formula, along with regular breast and pelvic exams as appropriate.
faqs: Why combine hormones in one preparation?
Using one product for several prescribed hormones can make a daily routine simpler. Your prescriber chooses the hormones, amounts and form.
Can children or pets be exposed to my hormone cream?
Yes, hormones on skin can transfer by touch. Let the area dry, cover it with clothing and wash your hands after applying.
How long before I notice changes?
Some people notice changes within a few weeks, while others take longer. Your prescriber may adjust the formula based on symptoms and lab results.

name: Cyanocobalamin (vitamin B12)
uses: Vitamin B12 supplement, including flavored liquids for pets.
how: Vitamin B12, needed for nerve function and red blood cells.
avoid: Usually well tolerated.
about: Cyanocobalamin is the most common supplement form of vitamin B12, which the body needs to make red blood cells, keep nerves healthy and make DNA. Low B12 can come from a limited diet, stomach or bowel problems, or certain medicines. In pets, it is often recommended for cats and dogs with chronic bowel or pancreas disease that lowers B12 levels. A flavored liquid makes daily oral dosing easier.
conditions: Low B12 in cats and dogs with bowel disease
Low B12 from long-term metformin or acid reducers
serious: Get medical or veterinary help right away for signs of an allergic reaction, such as hives, swelling or trouble breathing, which are rare.
interactions: Metformin, acid reducers such as omeprazole and famotidine, and colchicine can lower B12 absorption over time, which may be why it is prescribed. Give your prescriber, or your pet's veterinarian, a full list of medicines, supplements and flea or tick products.
pregnancy: Vitamin B12 is needed in pregnancy and breastfeeding and is included in prenatal vitamins; ask your prescriber before taking extra.
petNotes: Cats and dogs with chronic diarrhea, inflammatory bowel disease or exocrine pancreatic insufficiency often have low B12. A flavored liquid can be mixed with a small amount of food.
tips: Shake the liquid well before each dose.
Give it at about the same time each day.
It can be given with or without food.
If you miss a dose, take it when you remember unless it is almost time for the next one; don't double up.
monitoring: Your prescriber or veterinarian may recheck B12 levels to make sure the dose is meeting your or your pet's needs.
faqs: Can oral B12 work instead of injections?
For many people and pets, daily oral B12 can raise levels, though some still need injections. Your prescriber or veterinarian decides which is best.
Why do cats with bowel disease need B12?
B12 is absorbed in the lower small intestine, so bowel or pancreas disease can lead to low levels. Correcting it may help their overall condition.

name: Cyclosporine
uses: Immune-mediated disease and allergic skin disease in pets; dry eye.
how: Blocks activation of T cells, a key part of the immune response.
avoid: People or pets with cancer, serious infections, or kidney or liver disease.
about: Cyclosporine is an immunosuppressant first used in the 1980s to prevent organ transplant rejection. It calms the immune system by blocking T-cell activation. In veterinary medicine it is widely used for allergic skin disease in dogs and cats and for immune-mediated diseases, and as an eye ointment or drops for dry eye. Compounded forms can help with dosing small pets or pets that will not take capsules.
conditions: Atopic dermatitis in dogs and cats
serious: Get medical or veterinary help right away for fever, signs of infection, unusual lumps, yellow skin or eyes, decreased urination, severe vomiting or diarrhea, or seizures.
