name: Rosemary oil
uses: Ingredient in topical hair-growth serums.
how: A plant oil used in hair serums.
avoid: People with sensitive skin. Some essential oils are toxic to cats.
about: Rosemary oil is an essential oil from the rosemary plant. It has long been used in hair care, and interest has grown in it as an ingredient in scalp serums for thinning hair. Evidence is limited. Prescribers may order a compounded hair serum that combines rosemary oil with other ingredients such as ketoconazole or caffeine.
serious: Get medical help right away for signs of an allergic reaction such as hives, swelling of the face or throat, or trouble breathing, or for a blistering or spreading rash.
interactions: Interactions are unlikely when used on the scalp, but tell your prescriber about other scalp products you use. Give your prescriber a full list of medicines and supplements.
pregnancy: There is limited information on its use in pregnancy and breastfeeding, so ask your prescriber before using it if you are pregnant, planning pregnancy or breastfeeding.
tips: Apply to a dry or towel-dried scalp as directed and massage gently.
Test a small area first if you have sensitive skin.
Keep it out of your eyes, and wash your hands after applying.
Keep it away from pets, especially cats, and do not let them lick treated skin.
monitoring: Routine monitoring is usually not needed, but keep follow-up visits your prescriber schedules.
faqs: How long does rosemary oil take to work for hair?
Hair growth is slow, so any change usually takes several months of regular use.
Can I use pure rosemary essential oil on my scalp?
Undiluted essential oil can irritate the skin. Compounded serums are diluted and blended for scalp use.

name: Rutin
uses: Supplement used in cats and dogs with chylothorax (fluid around the lungs).
how: A plant flavonoid thought to help the body clear fluid from the chest in chylothorax.
avoid: Usually well tolerated.
about: Rutin is a natural plant flavonoid found in foods such as buckwheat and citrus. Veterinarians use it off-label as a supplement for cats and dogs with chylothorax, a condition in which a milky fluid builds up around the lungs. It may help the body clear the fluid, though the evidence is limited. A compounded flavored suspension can make it easier to give than tablets.
serious: Call your veterinarian right away for fast or labored breathing, open-mouth breathing in a cat, blue or pale gums, collapse or not eating.
interactions: Few drug interactions are known. Tell your veterinarian about every medicine, supplement and flea or tick product your pet gets.
petNotes: Rutin is usually one part of a plan that may include draining fluid, diet changes or surgery. Breathing trouble in cats is an emergency.
tips: Shake the suspension well before measuring.
It can be given with food.
Count your pet's breathing rate at rest and report increases to your veterinarian.
monitoring: Your veterinarian will usually recheck chest fluid with exams or X-rays.
faqs: How long does rutin take to help chylothorax?
It may take weeks to months to see a change, and not all pets respond. Your veterinarian will monitor fluid levels.
Is rutin safe for cats?
It is generally well tolerated in cats, but use only the product and dose your veterinarian prescribes.

name: Sacubitril/valsartan
uses: Heart failure.
side: Low blood pressure, dizziness, high potassium.
how: Combines a blocker of angiotensin receptors with a drug that preserves natural hormones that relax vessels and remove fluid.
avoid: Pregnancy, and anyone taking an ACE inhibitor or with a history of angioedema.
about: Sacubitril/valsartan combines valsartan, an angiotensin receptor blocker, with sacubitril, which preserves natural hormones that relax blood vessels and help remove extra fluid. Approved for people in 2015, it is a common part of treatment for heart failure. Veterinarians are exploring off-label use in dogs with heart disease. A compounded flavored suspension can help children or pets who need a smaller or liquid dose.
serious: Get medical or veterinary help right away for swelling of the face, lips, tongue or throat, fainting, a slow or uneven heartbeat, severe weakness, or much less urination.
interactions: Never take it with an ACE inhibitor or within 36 hours of one. Potassium supplements, potassium-sparing diuretics, aliskiren, NSAIDs and lithium can also interact. Give your prescriber, or your pet's veterinarian, a full list of medicines, supplements and flea or tick products.
pregnancy: Not used in pregnancy because it can harm a developing baby; talk to your prescriber if you are pregnant, planning pregnancy or breastfeeding.
petNotes: Use in dogs is off-label and still being studied. Your veterinarian will usually check kidney values and potassium after starting.
tips: Take or give it at the same times each day, with or without food.
Stand up slowly if you feel dizzy.
Avoid salt substitutes and potassium supplements unless your prescriber approves.
Shake the suspension well before measuring.
monitoring: Your prescriber or veterinarian will check blood pressure, kidney function and potassium levels.
faqs: Why can't I take Entresto with an ACE inhibitor?
Together they greatly raise the risk of angioedema, a dangerous swelling. A waiting period is needed when switching.
How long does sacubitril/valsartan take to work?
Some effects on symptoms may be felt within weeks, but benefits are judged over months.

name: Salicylic acid
uses: Warts, calluses and thick skin.
how: A beta hydroxy acid that softens and removes thick skin.
avoid: Large areas of skin, children, and people allergic to aspirin. Toxic to cats.
about: Salicylic acid is a beta hydroxy acid that has been used on the skin for more than a century. It softens and loosens the outer layer of skin, helping remove thick buildup. It is found in many over-the-counter wart, callus and acne products. Prescribers may order a compounded cream in a stronger or custom base, or combined with urea or fluorouracil for stubborn warts.
serious: Get medical help right away for ringing in the ears, nausea, fast breathing or confusion (possible salicylate toxicity), or for severe burning, blistering or signs of an allergic reaction.
interactions: Large amounts may add to the effects of aspirin, blood thinners and some diabetes medicines. Using other peeling products on the same area can increase irritation. Give your prescriber a full list of medicines and supplements.
pregnancy: Small areas are often considered low risk, but avoid large areas or long use and talk to your prescriber if you are pregnant, planning pregnancy or breastfeeding.
tips: Soak the area in warm water and pat dry before applying to help it absorb.
Apply only to the thick skin or wart, and protect the healthy skin around it.
Wash your hands after applying.
Keep treated skin away from pets, especially cats, and do not let them lick it.
monitoring: Routine monitoring is usually not needed, but keep follow-up visits your prescriber schedules.
faqs: How long does salicylic acid take to remove a wart?
Warts often take several weeks to a few months of regular use.
Can I use salicylic acid on my face?
Lower strengths are common in face products, but wart and callus creams are much stronger. Use only where your prescriber directs.
Should people with diabetes use salicylic acid on their feet?
People with diabetes or poor circulation should ask their prescriber first, since skin injuries on the feet can heal slowly.

name: SAM-e
uses: Liver and joint support supplement.
how: A natural compound that supports liver cell repair and joint health.
avoid: People with bipolar disorder or taking antidepressants.
about: SAM-e (S-adenosylmethionine) is a compound the body makes naturally and uses in many chemical reactions, including making glutathione, an antioxidant that helps protect liver cells. It is sold as a supplement for people and pets, and veterinarians often recommend it, sometimes with milk thistle, for liver support in dogs and cats. A compounded flavored suspension or capsule can help with dosing small pets.
conditions: Liver disease support in dogs and cats
serious: Get medical or veterinary help right away for signs of an allergic reaction, a racing heartbeat, severe restlessness or agitation, or yellow skin, eyes or gums.
interactions: It may add to the effects of antidepressants and other serotonin medicines, and should be used with care alongside levodopa. Give your prescriber, or your pet's veterinarian, a full list of medicines, supplements and flea or tick products.
pregnancy: There is not enough information on its safety in pregnancy and breastfeeding, so talk to your prescriber first.
petNotes: SAM-e is broken down by stomach acid and food, so it is usually given on an empty stomach and tablets are not split or crushed. A compounded form can make dosing easier for small pets.
tips: Give it on an empty stomach, about an hour before food, unless directed otherwise.
Keep capsules in their original container away from moisture and heat.
Shake suspensions well before measuring.
monitoring: Your prescriber or veterinarian may recheck liver blood work periodically.
faqs: Why is SAM-e given on an empty stomach?
Food can reduce how much is absorbed, so it is usually given about an hour before a meal.
Is SAM-e safe for dogs and cats?
It is commonly recommended by veterinarians and is generally well tolerated. Use only the product and dose your veterinarian recommends.

name: Topical sildenafil combination cream for women
uses: A prescription cream for women with sexual arousal concerns, combining theophylline, ergoloid mesylates, pentoxifylline and sildenafil (sometimes with L-arginine), as prescribed.
side: Warmth, tingling or redness where applied, and occasional headache.
how: Each ingredient increases local blood flow in a different way.
avoid: Anyone taking nitrates for chest pain, and people with low blood pressure or an allergy to any ingredient. Not for use during pregnancy.
about: This compounded cream combines several ingredients that increase blood flow, including sildenafil, theophylline, pentoxifylline and ergoloid mesylates, sometimes with L-arginine. Each works in a different way to support local circulation. No commercial product contains this combination, and its use for female sexual arousal concerns is off-label with limited evidence. Prescribers may order it for women with arousal or sensitivity concerns.
serious: Get medical help right away for chest pain, fainting, severe dizziness, sudden vision or hearing changes, or signs of an allergic reaction such as hives or swelling of the face or throat.
interactions: Never use with nitrates for chest pain or with riociguat. Use caution with blood pressure medicines, alpha blockers and medicines that raise theophylline levels. Give your prescriber a full list of medicines and supplements.
pregnancy: Not for use during pregnancy; talk to your prescriber if you are pregnant, planning pregnancy or breastfeeding.
tips: Apply only the small amount your prescriber directs to the area recommended.
Wash your hands after applying.
Stop and call your prescriber if you notice strong burning, a rash or lasting dizziness.
monitoring: Routine monitoring is usually not needed, but keep follow-up visits your prescriber schedules.
faqs: How soon before intimacy is the cream applied?
Timing varies, so follow your prescriber's directions.
Can partners be affected by the cream?
Small amounts could transfer during contact. Ask your prescriber about timing and whether to wash the area.

name: Selegiline
uses: Cognitive dysfunction in older dogs and pituitary-dependent Cushing's.
how: Blocks MAO-B, an enzyme that breaks down dopamine in the brain.
avoid: Pets taking other behavior medicines such as fluoxetine or amitriptyline, or certain flea and tick products (amitraz).
about: Selegiline is a monoamine oxidase type B (MAO-B) inhibitor first used in people with Parkinson's disease. A veterinary brand was later approved for dogs with canine cognitive dysfunction and some cases of pituitary-dependent Cushing's disease. Veterinarians may ask for it compounded when a dog needs a strength that commercial tablets don't offer or a capsule that is easier to give.
conditions: Senior dog confusion and night waking
serious: Call your veterinarian right away for severe agitation, trembling, a very fast heartbeat, collapse, or vomiting or diarrhea that does not stop.
interactions: Combining selegiline with other behavior medicines such as SSRIs or tricyclic antidepressants, with some opioid pain medicines, or with amitraz tick collars and dips can cause a dangerous serotonin reaction. Tell your veterinarian about every medicine, supplement and flea or tick product your pet gets.
petNotes: Selegiline is used mainly in dogs; use in cats is less common and is decided by the veterinarian. Morning dosing is often preferred because it can cause restlessness at night.
tips: Give it in the morning unless your veterinarian says otherwise, since evening doses may disturb sleep.
It can take several weeks to see changes in behavior, so keep a simple diary of sleep, accidents and confusion to share with your vet.
If a dose is missed, give or take it when you remember unless it is almost time for the next dose; don't double up.
monitoring: Your veterinarian will check how your dog's behavior and Cushing's signs respond and may run blood work before and during treatment.
faqs: How long does selegiline take to work in dogs?
Many owners notice changes over a few weeks, and the full effect may take longer. Your veterinarian may reassess after a trial period.
Can my dog wear a tick collar while taking selegiline?
Collars and dips that contain amitraz should not be used with selegiline. Ask your veterinarian which flea and tick products are safe.
Is selegiline used for Cushing's in all dogs?
No. It is considered only for some dogs with uncomplicated pituitary-dependent Cushing's, and your veterinarian decides whether it fits your dog.

name: Sertraline
uses: Anxiety and depression; behavior problems in pets.
how: An SSRI that increases serotonin available in the brain.
avoid: Anyone taking MAO inhibitors or other serotonin medicines.
about: Sertraline is a selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor (SSRI) that has been widely prescribed for depression and anxiety disorders since the early 1990s. Veterinarians also use it off-label for anxiety and some compulsive behaviors in dogs and cats. A compounded capsule can provide a smaller strength for a pet or for someone who needs a dose that commercial tablets don't provide.
conditions: Anxiety behaviors in dogs and cats
serious: Get medical or veterinary help right away for new or worsening thoughts of suicide, agitation, high fever with stiff muscles or shaking, seizures, unusual bleeding, or signs of an allergic reaction.
interactions: Avoid MAO inhibitors (including selegiline and amitraz tick products in pets), some opioid pain medicines, triptans, linezolid and other serotonin medicines, and use care with blood thinners and NSAIDs, which raise bleeding risk. Give your prescriber, or your pet's veterinarian, a full list of medicines, supplements and flea or tick products.
pregnancy: Sertraline is sometimes used in pregnancy and breastfeeding when the benefits outweigh the risks; talk to your prescriber before you start, stop or change it if you are pregnant, planning pregnancy or breastfeeding.
petNotes: In pets it is used off-label, usually together with behavior training, and it may take several weeks to show an effect. Cats and dogs metabolize it differently, so the veterinarian sets the dose for the species.
tips: Take or give it at the same time each day, with or without food; food may ease stomach upset.
Do not stop it suddenly; your prescriber or veterinarian can taper it to avoid withdrawal effects.
If a dose is missed, give or take it when you remember unless it is almost time for the next dose; don't double up.
monitoring: Your prescriber or veterinarian will follow up on mood or behavior, especially in the first weeks and after any dose change, and may check liver values in pets on long-term use.
faqs: How long does sertraline take to work?
Some changes may appear in one to two weeks, but the full effect often takes four to six weeks or longer, in people and in pets.
Can I drink alcohol while taking sertraline?
Alcohol can add to drowsiness and may worsen depression or anxiety, so most prescribers advise avoiding it or limiting it.
Is sertraline safe for dogs and cats?
Veterinarians do prescribe it off-label for anxiety in dogs and cats. Use only the dose your vet prescribes and never give a pet a person's tablets.

name: Sildenafil
uses: Erectile dysfunction and topical sexual-health creams in people; pulmonary hypertension in dogs and cats.
side: Headache, flushing, nasal congestion, low blood pressure. Do not combine with nitrates.
how: Blocks PDE5, an enzyme that narrows blood vessels, which improves blood flow in the penis and lungs.
avoid: Anyone taking nitrates for chest pain or certain blood pressure medicines, and people with severe heart disease or very low blood pressure.
about: Sildenafil is a phosphodiesterase type 5 (PDE5) inhibitor that became widely known in the late 1990s for erectile dysfunction and is also used for pulmonary arterial hypertension. Veterinarians use it off-label for pulmonary hypertension in dogs and cats. Compounding allows flavored liquids for pets, troches, and topical creams used off-label in sexual health.
serious: Get medical or veterinary help right away for chest pain, fainting, an erection lasting more than 4 hours, sudden vision or hearing loss, or signs of an allergic reaction such as swelling or trouble breathing.
interactions: Never combine with nitrates (such as nitroglycerin or recreational poppers) or riociguat, and use caution with alpha-blockers, other blood pressure medicines, and drugs that raise sildenafil levels such as certain antifungals, HIV medicines and macrolide antibiotics. Give your prescriber, or your pet's veterinarian, a full list of medicines, supplements and flea or tick products.
pregnancy: Sildenafil is not expected to be used for sexual health in pregnancy, and for other uses your prescriber weighs risks and benefits; talk to your prescriber if you are pregnant, planning pregnancy or breastfeeding.
petNotes: Flavored oral suspensions make dosing easier for small dogs and cats with pulmonary hypertension, a use that is off-label. Watch for flushing of the ears or belly, weakness or fainting, and tell your vet.
tips: For erectile dysfunction, a heavy, high-fat meal can delay how fast it works.
Shake liquid forms well before each dose and measure with the syringe or cup provided.
Wash hands after applying cream and follow your prescriber's directions for where and how much to apply.
monitoring: Routine lab monitoring is usually not needed for people, but pets with pulmonary hypertension often have follow-up exams and heart ultrasounds with their veterinarian.
faqs: How long does sildenafil last?
For erectile dysfunction its effect generally lasts about four hours. Tadalafil, a related medicine, lasts longer.
Can I drink alcohol with sildenafil?
Small amounts are usually not a problem, but heavy drinking can lower blood pressure and make it harder to get an erection.
Why would a dog take sildenafil?
Veterinarians use it off-label to relax blood vessels in the lungs in dogs with pulmonary hypertension, which may ease breathing and help with fainting episodes.

name: Sirolimus
uses: Immune suppression and some specialty uses.
how: Blocks mTOR, a signal that drives immune cell and tissue growth.
avoid: People with serious infections or poor wound healing.
about: Sirolimus, also called rapamycin, is an mTOR inhibitor first approved in the late 1990s to help prevent organ transplant rejection. It is also used for some rare conditions and specialty uses decided by a specialist, some of them off-label. A compounded capsule may be requested for a strength or dosage form that is not available commercially, in people or occasionally in pets under specialist care.
conditions: Specialty uses decided by a specialist
serious: Get medical or veterinary help right away for fever, chills or other signs of infection, swelling in the legs or face, shortness of breath or new cough, unusual bleeding, or a wound that will not heal.
interactions: Sirolimus levels are strongly affected by drugs that change the CYP3A4 liver enzyme, such as ketoconazole, itraconazole, clarithromycin, rifampin, and some seizure medicines, as well as grapefruit juice; live vaccines should be avoided. Give your prescriber, or your pet's veterinarian, a full list of medicines, supplements and flea or tick products.
pregnancy: Sirolimus is generally avoided in pregnancy and breastfeeding, and effective birth control is usually advised during treatment and for some weeks afterward; talk to your prescriber if you are pregnant, planning pregnancy or breastfeeding.
petNotes: Use in dogs and cats is off-label and specialized, so dosing and blood work are directed by the veterinarian or specialist. Wear gloves when handling capsules, and keep them away from other pets and children.
tips: Take it the same way every time, either always with food or always without, so blood levels stay steady.
Avoid grapefruit and grapefruit juice while taking sirolimus.
Use sunscreen and protective clothing, since sirolimus may raise the risk of skin cancer with sun exposure.
monitoring: Your prescriber will usually check sirolimus blood levels, blood counts, cholesterol and triglycerides, kidney function and urine protein on a regular schedule.
faqs: Is sirolimus the same as rapamycin?
Yes. Sirolimus is the drug name for rapamycin, a compound first found in soil bacteria from Easter Island (Rapa Nui).
Why does sirolimus need blood tests?
The amount in the blood can vary a lot between people and with other medicines, so prescribers often measure levels to keep them in the intended range.

name: Sodium butyrate
uses: Suppositories used for bowel inflammation such as proctitis.
how: A short-chain fatty acid that is the main fuel for cells lining the colon.
avoid: People with rectal bleeding that has not been evaluated.
about: Sodium butyrate is the sodium salt of butyrate, a short-chain fatty acid that gut bacteria normally make when they break down fiber. Cells lining the colon use butyrate as their main energy source, and researchers have studied rectal butyrate for inflammation of the lower bowel. There is no commercial prescription suppository in the US, so prescribers who want to try it, an off-label use, ask for it compounded.
conditions: Ulcerative colitis of the lower bowel
serious: Get medical help right away for heavy rectal bleeding, severe belly pain, fever, or signs of an allergic reaction such as hives, swelling or trouble breathing.
interactions: Sodium butyrate suppositories act locally and have few known drug interactions; use other rectal products only as your prescriber directs. Give your prescriber a full list of medicines and supplements.
pregnancy: There is little information on sodium butyrate suppositories in pregnancy or breastfeeding; talk to your prescriber if you are pregnant, planning pregnancy or breastfeeding.
tips: Empty your bowels before inserting a suppository if you can, so it stays in place longer.
Store suppositories as labeled, and if one softens, chill it briefly before unwrapping.
Butyrate has a strong odor; this is normal and does not mean the product has gone bad.
monitoring: Your prescriber will follow your symptoms and may repeat a scope exam to see how the bowel lining is healing.
faqs: How do I insert a suppository?
Wash your hands, unwrap it, lie on your side with your top knee bent, and gently push it into the rectum pointed end first. Stay lying down for a few minutes afterward.
Is sodium butyrate the same as butyrate supplements I can buy?
They contain the same compound, but oral supplements are mostly absorbed before reaching the lower colon. Rectal suppositories deliver it directly to the area being treated.

name: Sotalol
uses: Heart rhythm disorders in people and dogs.
how: A beta-blocker with extra effects on the heart's electrical rhythm.
avoid: People or pets with asthma, slow heart rate or kidney disease; requires careful monitoring.
about: Sotalol is a heart rhythm medicine that combines beta-blocking effects with class III antiarrhythmic action, which lengthens the heart's electrical recharge time. It has been used in people since the early 1990s and is used off-label by veterinarians, especially for ventricular arrhythmias in dogs such as Boxer cardiomyopathy. A flavored suspension or custom capsule helps when a dog needs a strength that tablets don't provide.
serious: Get medical or veterinary help right away for fainting, a very slow, fast or pounding heartbeat, chest pain, trouble breathing, or swelling of the legs or belly.
interactions: Avoid combining with other medicines that prolong the QT interval (such as some antibiotics, antidepressants and antipsychotics), other antiarrhythmics, calcium channel blockers like diltiazem or verapamil, and antacids taken within two hours. Give your prescriber, or your pet's veterinarian, a full list of medicines, supplements and flea or tick products.
pregnancy: Sotalol is sometimes used in pregnancy when needed for heart rhythm control, and it passes into breast milk; talk to your prescriber if you are pregnant, planning pregnancy or breastfeeding.
petNotes: In dogs, sotalol is used off-label and is often started with an ECG or Holter monitor to judge the response. Do not stop it suddenly, since rebound rhythm problems can occur.
tips: Give it at evenly spaced times each day, and keep it separated from antacids by at least two hours.
Do not stop sotalol suddenly; your prescriber or veterinarian will taper it if needed.
Shake the suspension well and measure with an oral syringe.
monitoring: Your prescriber or veterinarian will check ECGs (heart tracings), kidney function, and potassium and magnesium levels, especially when starting or changing the dose.
faqs: Why do people start sotalol in the hospital?
Sotalol can cause a dangerous rhythm change in some people, so prescribers often start it with ECG monitoring for a few days.
Is sotalol a beta-blocker?
Yes, but it also has antiarrhythmic effects that typical beta-blockers like metoprolol don't have, so it is not interchangeable with them.

name: Spironolactone
uses: Heart failure and fluid buildup; hormonal acne and hair loss in women.
side: High potassium, breast tenderness, irregular periods.
how: Blocks the hormone aldosterone, helping the body shed fluid while holding onto potassium; also blocks some androgen effects.
avoid: People or pets with high potassium or kidney disease, and those who are pregnant.
about: Spironolactone is a potassium-sparing diuretic that blocks aldosterone, a hormone that makes the body hold on to salt and water. It has been used since around 1960 for heart failure and fluid buildup and is often prescribed off-label for hormonal acne and hair thinning in women because of its anti-androgen effects. Compounded forms include flavored liquids for pets and topical creams and foams for skin and scalp.
serious: Get medical or veterinary help right away for muscle weakness, a slow or irregular heartbeat (possible high potassium), severe dizziness or fainting, very little urine, or signs of an allergic reaction.
interactions: Avoid potassium supplements and salt substitutes unless prescribed, and use care with ACE inhibitors, ARBs (such as telmisartan), NSAIDs, trimethoprim and lithium, which can raise potassium or affect kidney function. Give your prescriber, or your pet's veterinarian, a full list of medicines, supplements and flea or tick products.
pregnancy: Spironolactone is not used in pregnancy because its anti-androgen effects could affect a developing baby; talk to your prescriber if you are pregnant, planning pregnancy or breastfeeding.
petNotes: In dogs it is often used together with other heart medicines; in cats it can occasionally cause facial skin irritation, so report scratching or scabs. Flavored suspensions make dosing small pets easier.
tips: Oral forms are best taken with food and at the same time each day.
Morning doses help avoid getting up at night to urinate.
For topical cream or foam, apply to clean, dry skin or scalp and wash your hands afterward.
monitoring: With oral spironolactone, your prescriber or veterinarian will check potassium and kidney function periodically, especially when starting or changing the dose.
faqs: How long does spironolactone take to work for acne?
Many people need about two to three months to see a clear change, and hair benefits may take longer.
Does topical spironolactone cause high potassium?
Topical forms are applied to the skin and are expected to reach the bloodstream in much smaller amounts than tablets, but your prescriber decides whether lab checks are needed.
Do men take spironolactone for acne?
Usually not, because its anti-androgen effects can cause breast enlargement in men. It is mainly used for acne in women.

name: Sucralfate
uses: Coats and protects ulcers and irritated tissue; used in mouthwash blends.
how: Forms a protective coating over ulcers and irritated tissue.
avoid: Give 2 hours apart from other medicines, since it can block their absorption.
about: Sucralfate is a gastrointestinal protectant made from sucrose and aluminum. In acid it becomes a sticky paste that binds to damaged tissue and shields it from acid, bile and enzymes. It has been used since the 1980s for ulcers, and prescribers and veterinarians may order it compounded into a mouthwash or rinse to coat painful mouth or throat sores, an off-label use.
conditions: Mouth sores from chemotherapy or radiation
Esophageal and stomach ulcers in dogs and cats
serious: Get medical or veterinary help right away for signs of an allergic reaction such as hives, swelling of the face or throat, or trouble breathing.
interactions: Sucralfate can bind other medicines and reduce their absorption, including fluoroquinolone antibiotics, thyroid hormone, digoxin, phenytoin and warfarin, so space them apart; avoid aluminum antacids in people with kidney disease. Give your prescriber, or your pet's veterinarian, a full list of medicines, supplements and flea or tick products.
pregnancy: Sucralfate is only slightly absorbed and is generally considered low risk in pregnancy and breastfeeding; talk to your prescriber if you are pregnant, planning pregnancy or breastfeeding.
petNotes: Veterinarians use sucralfate off-label in dogs and cats with esophagitis or ulcers, and it should be spaced from other oral medicines. A liquid form is easier to give than crushed tablets.
tips: Shake the mouthwash well and swish or coat the mouth as directed; ask whether to spit it out or swallow it.
Avoid eating or drinking for a short time after using it so the coating can stay in place.
Space other medicines from sucralfate as your pharmacist or prescriber advises.
monitoring: Routine monitoring is usually not needed, but keep follow-up visits your prescriber or veterinarian schedules, and people with kidney disease may have aluminum levels checked with long-term use.
faqs: Should I swallow sucralfate mouthwash or spit it out?
It depends on what it is treating. Rinses for mouth sores may be spit out, while those for throat or esophagus sores are often swallowed, so follow your label.
Why must sucralfate be spaced from other medicines?
It forms a coating that can trap other drugs in the gut, so they may not be absorbed as well if taken at the same time.

name: Sulfamethoxazole/trimethoprim
uses: Urinary, skin and other infections.
side: Stomach upset, dry eye in dogs, allergic reaction.
how: Two drugs that block bacteria from making folic acid.
avoid: Anyone with a sulfa allergy, liver disease or dry eye (dogs), and Doberman pinschers.
about: Sulfamethoxazole/trimethoprim is a combination antibiotic in use since the late 1960s that blocks two steps of folic acid production in bacteria. It treats a range of urinary, skin, respiratory and other infections in people, and veterinarians use similar sulfa combinations in dogs and cats. Compounding can provide flavored suspensions, powders, ear packs or nasal sprays when a standard tablet or liquid does not fit the patient.
conditions: Urinary and skin infections in dogs
serious: Get medical or veterinary help right away for a spreading rash or blistering, fever with sores in the mouth, yellow skin or eyes, unusual bruising or bleeding, joint swelling, or severe watery diarrhea.
interactions: Use caution with warfarin, methotrexate, phenytoin, some diabetes medicines (sulfonylureas), and drugs that raise potassium such as ACE inhibitors, ARBs and spironolactone. Give your prescriber, or your pet's veterinarian, a full list of medicines, supplements and flea or tick products.
pregnancy: It is generally avoided in pregnancy, especially early and near delivery, and in breastfeeding newborns; talk to your prescriber if you are pregnant, planning pregnancy or breastfeeding.
petNotes: Dogs can develop dry eye, joint pain, rash or liver problems, and Doberman pinschers seem especially prone to sulfa reactions. Cats often dislike the taste, so flavored forms may help.
tips: Take or give oral forms with a full glass of water (or encourage your pet to drink), to help protect the kidneys.
Finish the full course even if signs improve, unless your prescriber tells you to stop.
Use sunscreen, since it can make skin more sensitive to sunlight.
monitoring: For longer courses, your prescriber may check blood counts, kidney function and potassium, and veterinarians often run tear tests in dogs to watch for dry eye.
faqs: Is SMX-TMP a sulfa drug?
Yes. The sulfamethoxazole part is a sulfonamide, so people or pets with a sulfa allergy should not take it.
Can I drink alcohol with sulfamethoxazole/trimethoprim?
Alcohol may add to stomach upset and is best avoided while you are fighting an infection; ask your prescriber.
What should I watch for in my dog?
Watch for red, goopy or dry eyes, limping, rash, fever or yellow gums, and call your veterinarian if you see them.

name: T4/T3 thyroid capsules
uses: Levothyroxine (T4) and liothyronine (T3) combined in one capsule, in the strengths and ratio your prescriber orders, including slow-release capsules.
side: Signs of too much thyroid hormone: fast heartbeat, anxiety, trouble sleeping, sweating or weight loss.
how: T4 is the storage form of thyroid hormone that the body converts into active T3. A combination capsule replaces both hormones together.
avoid: People with heart disease or untreated adrenal insufficiency. Your prescriber adjusts the dose based on your lab results.
about: T4/T3 thyroid capsules combine levothyroxine (synthetic T4) and liothyronine (synthetic T3) in one capsule. Some prescribers choose combination therapy for people who still have symptoms on T4 alone, and the ratio of the two hormones is set by the prescriber. A commercial combination product (liotrix) was discontinued, so prescribers who want a single capsule, including slow-release versions, ask for it compounded.
serious: Get medical help right away for chest pain, a racing or irregular heartbeat, shortness of breath, severe headache, or signs of an allergic reaction.
interactions: Calcium, iron, antacids, sucralfate, cholestyramine, soy and high-fiber meals can block absorption, and thyroid hormone can change the effect of warfarin and diabetes medicines. Give your prescriber a full list of medicines and supplements.
pregnancy: Thyroid hormone is continued in pregnancy and breastfeeding, but needs often change, so tell your prescriber right away if you become pregnant or are planning pregnancy.
tips: Take it at the same time each day, usually on an empty stomach with water, unless your prescriber says otherwise.
Separate it from calcium, iron and antacids by at least four hours.
Do not open slow-release capsules, and avoid switching between products without telling your prescriber.
monitoring: Your prescriber will check thyroid blood tests (such as TSH, free T4 and free T3) several weeks after starting or changing the dose and periodically after that.
faqs: Why take T4 and T3 together?
Most people do well on T4 alone, but some prescribers try adding T3 for people who still have symptoms. Your prescriber decides whether it fits you.
What does a slow-release capsule do?
It is designed to release the T3 more gradually during the day, which may smooth out peaks in hormone levels.
Should I take my capsule before my blood test?
Ask your prescriber, because T3 can raise levels for a few hours after a dose and some prescribers want you to wait until after the blood draw.

name: Tacrolimus
uses: Immune-related skin and eye conditions.
how: Blocks activation of T cells in the skin or eye.
avoid: People or pets with active skin infections.
about: Tacrolimus is a calcineurin inhibitor that calms overactive immune cells. Taken by mouth it helps prevent transplant rejection, and as an ointment it is approved for eczema. Prescribers and veterinarians use topical and eye forms for skin and eye conditions such as dry eye in dogs, often off-label, and may ask for it compounded when a strength or base is not available commercially.
serious: Get medical or veterinary help right away for signs of skin or eye infection (pus, spreading redness, severe pain), swollen glands, new lumps or skin growths, or signs of an allergic reaction.
interactions: Topical and eye forms have few interactions because little reaches the blood, but avoid using other strong topical immune-suppressing products on the same area unless directed; oral tacrolimus interacts with many drugs. Give your prescriber, or your pet's veterinarian, a full list of medicines, supplements and flea or tick products.
pregnancy: Little topical tacrolimus reaches the blood, but its safety in pregnancy and breastfeeding is not well established; talk to your prescriber if you are pregnant, planning pregnancy or breastfeeding.
petNotes: Tacrolimus eye drops or ointment are used off-label in dogs with dry eye that has not responded to other treatments. Wear gloves when applying it to your pet and wash hands afterward.
tips: Apply a thin layer only to the affected area, and wash your hands afterward unless your hands are being treated.
Burning or stinging usually fades after the first week or two of use.
Limit sun and tanning bed exposure on treated skin.
Alcohol may cause facial flushing in some people using topical tacrolimus.
monitoring: Routine lab monitoring is usually not needed for topical or eye use, but keep follow-up visits, and dogs with dry eye usually have repeat tear tests.
faqs: What is the difference between tacrolimus and cyclosporine eye drops for dogs?
Both calm the immune response that damages tear glands. Tacrolimus is sometimes tried when cyclosporine has not helped enough; your veterinarian decides.
Why does tacrolimus sting at first?
Stinging and warmth are common in the first days of use and usually get better as the skin adjusts. Tell your prescriber if it is severe.
Is topical tacrolimus a steroid?
No. It works differently and does not cause the skin thinning that long-term steroid creams can.

name: Tadalafil
uses: Erectile dysfunction, enlarged prostate symptoms and pulmonary hypertension.
side: Headache, flushing, back pain, low blood pressure. Do not combine with nitrates.
how: Blocks PDE5, relaxing smooth muscle and improving blood flow; it lasts longer than sildenafil.
avoid: Anyone taking nitrates for chest pain, and people with severe heart disease or very low blood pressure.
about: Tadalafil is a long-acting phosphodiesterase type 5 (PDE5) inhibitor used since 2003 for erectile dysfunction and later for urinary symptoms of an enlarged prostate and for pulmonary arterial hypertension. Its effects last longer than sildenafil's. Compounded troches and oral liquids may be requested for people who prefer them or have trouble swallowing tablets, and veterinarians sometimes use it off-label for pulmonary hypertension in dogs.
serious: Get medical or veterinary help right away for chest pain, fainting, an erection lasting more than 4 hours, sudden vision or hearing loss, or signs of an allergic reaction.
interactions: Never combine with nitrates (such as nitroglycerin or poppers) or riociguat, and use caution with alpha-blockers, other blood pressure medicines, and drugs that raise tadalafil levels such as certain antifungals and HIV medicines. Give your prescriber, or your pet's veterinarian, a full list of medicines, supplements and flea or tick products.
pregnancy: Tadalafil is not expected to be used for sexual health in pregnancy, and for other uses your prescriber weighs risks and benefits; talk to your prescriber if you are pregnant, planning pregnancy or breastfeeding.
petNotes: Veterinarians may use tadalafil off-label in dogs with pulmonary hypertension because it can be given less often than sildenafil. Watch for weakness, flushing or fainting, and tell your vet.
tips: It can be taken with or without food.
Let a troche dissolve between the cheek and gum without chewing or swallowing it whole.
Limit alcohol, which can add to dizziness and low blood pressure.
monitoring: Routine lab monitoring is usually not needed, but keep follow-up visits your prescriber schedules, and people or pets with pulmonary hypertension have regular heart and lung checks.
faqs: How long does tadalafil last?
Its effects can last up to about 36 hours.
What is the difference between tadalafil and sildenafil?
Both are PDE5 inhibitors. Tadalafil lasts longer and is less affected by food, while sildenafil has a shorter effect; your prescriber chooses which fits.
Does tadalafil help prostate symptoms?
It is prescribed for urinary symptoms of an enlarged prostate, such as weak flow or frequent urination, and may help in some men.

name: Tamsulosin
uses: Urinary flow problems from an enlarged prostate or urethral spasm.
how: Relaxes muscle in the prostate and bladder neck to improve urine flow.
avoid: People or pets with low blood pressure; people with a sulfa allergy should check with their prescriber.
about: Tamsulosin is an alpha-1 blocker that relaxes smooth muscle in the prostate and bladder neck. It has been used since the late 1990s for urinary symptoms of an enlarged prostate and is sometimes used off-label to help pass kidney stones. Veterinarians use it off-label for urethral spasm in dogs and cats, and a flavored suspension helps when capsules cannot be opened or a smaller dose is needed.
serious: Get medical or veterinary help right away for fainting, a painful erection lasting more than 4 hours, a severe skin rash, or signs of an allergic reaction.
interactions: Use caution with other alpha-blockers, PDE5 inhibitors such as sildenafil or tadalafil, blood pressure medicines, and drugs that raise tamsulosin levels such as ketoconazole. Give your prescriber, or your pet's veterinarian, a full list of medicines, supplements and flea or tick products.
pregnancy: Tamsulosin is not intended for use in women, and its safety in pregnancy and breastfeeding has not been established; talk to your prescriber if you are pregnant, planning pregnancy or breastfeeding.
petNotes: In male cats after a urinary blockage, tamsulosin may be used off-label to relax the urethra; watch closely for straining or no urine, which is an emergency. Dizziness may show as wobbliness in pets.
tips: Take it at the same time each day, usually after the same meal.
Stand up slowly, especially after the first doses, to avoid dizziness.
Tell your eye surgeon you take or have taken tamsulosin before any cataract surgery.
monitoring: Routine lab monitoring is usually not needed, but your prescriber or veterinarian will follow urinary symptoms and may check blood pressure.
faqs: How fast does tamsulosin work?
Some people notice better urine flow within a few days, though it may take a few weeks for the full effect.
Why does tamsulosin matter for cataract surgery?
It can cause floppy iris syndrome, which makes eye surgery harder, so your eye surgeon needs to know even if you stopped it.
Can cats take tamsulosin?
Veterinarians sometimes prescribe it off-label for cats with urethral spasm. Use only a pet-specific dose from your vet.

name: Telmisartan
uses: High blood pressure in people and cats and kidney protein loss.
side: Dizziness, low blood pressure, changes in kidney values.
how: Blocks angiotensin receptors, relaxing blood vessels and protecting the kidneys.
avoid: Pregnancy, and people or pets with dehydration or high potassium.
about: Telmisartan is an angiotensin II receptor blocker (ARB) used since the late 1990s for high blood pressure in people. A veterinary oral solution is approved for cats with high blood pressure and for protein loss in the urine from chronic kidney disease, and it is used off-label in dogs. Compounded suspensions or capsules may be requested for dogs, cats or people who need a different strength or flavor.
serious: Get medical or veterinary help right away for fainting, very little urine, muscle weakness or slow heartbeat (possible high potassium), or swelling of the face, lips or throat.
interactions: Use caution with ACE inhibitors, aliskiren, potassium supplements, salt substitutes, spironolactone, NSAIDs and lithium, which can affect potassium or kidney function. Give your prescriber, or your pet's veterinarian, a full list of medicines, supplements and flea or tick products.
pregnancy: Telmisartan can harm a developing baby and should be stopped as soon as pregnancy is known; talk to your prescriber if you are pregnant, planning pregnancy or breastfeeding.
petNotes: Cats usually accept flavored liquids well, and dosing is based on weight. Make sure your pet is eating and drinking normally, since dehydration raises the risk of kidney problems.
tips: Take or give it at the same time each day, with or without food.
Shake liquid forms well before measuring each dose.
Call your prescriber or veterinarian if vomiting or diarrhea leads to dehydration.
monitoring: Your prescriber or veterinarian will check blood pressure, kidney values and potassium periodically, and urine protein in pets with kidney disease.
faqs: How is telmisartan different from an ACE inhibitor?
Both act on the same hormone system, but ARBs block the receptor rather than the enzyme and are less likely to cause a dry cough.
Can telmisartan be used in dogs?
Yes, veterinarians use it off-label in dogs, often for protein in the urine from kidney disease.
How long does telmisartan take to lower blood pressure?
Blood pressure often starts to drop within the first couple of weeks, with fuller effect after about four weeks.

name: Terbinafine
uses: Fungal skin and nail infections, including ringworm.
how: Blocks squalene epoxidase, an enzyme fungi need to build their membranes.
avoid: People or pets with liver or kidney disease.
about: Terbinafine is an allylamine antifungal used since the early 1990s for fungal infections of the skin, hair and nails, including ringworm. Taken by mouth it builds up in nails and skin, which is why it is often chosen for nail fungus. Veterinarians use it off-label for ringworm and some other fungal infections in dogs and cats, and a flavored suspension makes dosing small animals easier.
conditions: Ringworm of the scalp or body
serious: Get medical or veterinary help right away for yellow skin or eyes, dark urine, pale stools, loss of appetite with vomiting, a severe rash or blisters, or a sudden change in mood or taste that does not go away.
interactions: Terbinafine can raise levels of some antidepressants, beta-blockers and other drugs broken down by the CYP2D6 enzyme, and rifampin or cimetidine can change terbinafine levels. Give your prescriber, or your pet's veterinarian, a full list of medicines, supplements and flea or tick products.
pregnancy: Oral terbinafine is usually postponed until after pregnancy because fungal nail infections are not urgent; talk to your prescriber if you are pregnant, planning pregnancy or breastfeeding.
petNotes: It is used off-label in dogs and cats, often together with medicated baths for ringworm. Ringworm can spread to people, so wash hands after handling an infected pet.
tips: Shake the suspension well before each dose.
Treatment can take weeks to months; keep giving it for the full time prescribed, even when skin looks better.
Clean bedding and grooming tools regularly to help stop ringworm spreading.
monitoring: Your prescriber or veterinarian may check liver values before and during longer treatment, and pets with ringworm often have repeat fungal cultures.
faqs: How long does terbinafine take to clear nail fungus?
Nails grow slowly, so it may take several months after treatment ends to see a fully clear nail.
Can I catch ringworm from my cat?
Yes, ringworm can spread between pets and people. Wash hands after handling your pet and see your own doctor if you notice a ring-shaped rash.
Can I drink alcohol with terbinafine?
Because terbinafine is processed by the liver, many prescribers advise limiting alcohol during treatment.

name: Terbutaline
uses: Opens airways in asthma and feline asthma.
how: Relaxes airway muscles by stimulating beta-2 receptors.
avoid: People or pets with heart rhythm problems, high blood pressure or overactive thyroid.
about: Terbutaline is a beta-2 agonist bronchodilator that relaxes the muscles around the airways. It has been used since the 1970s for asthma and similar breathing conditions, and the brand tablet has been discontinued. Veterinarians use it off-label for feline asthma and some airway diseases in dogs, and compounded flavored suspensions or capsules help with small or hard-to-pill pets.
serious: Get medical or veterinary help right away for chest pain, a racing or irregular heartbeat, severe trembling, seizures, or breathing that gets worse instead of better.
interactions: Beta-blockers can block terbutaline's effect, and use caution with other stimulant or airway medicines, MAO inhibitors, tricyclic antidepressants and diuretics that lower potassium. Give your prescriber, or your pet's veterinarian, a full list of medicines, supplements and flea or tick products.
pregnancy: Terbutaline should not be used by mouth to prevent or treat preterm labor because of serious heart risks to the mother; talk to your prescriber if you are pregnant, planning pregnancy or breastfeeding.
petNotes: A cat with open-mouth breathing or blue gums is having an emergency and needs to be seen right away. Hyperactivity or a fast heart rate in pets can mean the dose is too high.
tips: Shake the suspension well and measure each dose with the syringe provided.
Keep a note of breathing episodes so your prescriber or veterinarian can judge how well it is working.
If a dose is missed, give or take it when you remember unless it is almost time for the next dose; don't double up.
monitoring: Your prescriber or veterinarian will follow breathing symptoms and heart rate, and may check potassium or blood sugar in some patients.
faqs: Is terbutaline a rescue medicine?
Oral forms take longer to work than inhaled rescue medicines, so they are usually used for ongoing control. Ask your prescriber or vet about an emergency plan.
Can cats take terbutaline?
Veterinarians commonly prescribe it off-label for feline asthma, sometimes along with inhaled or oral steroids.

name: Terconazole
uses: Vaginal yeast infections.
how: Blocks fungal cell membrane production.
avoid: Usually well tolerated; for vaginal use only.
about: Terconazole is a triazole antifungal used in the vagina to treat yeast infections caused by Candida. Commercial vaginal creams and suppositories have been available in the US since the 1980s. A prescriber may ask for a compounded cream when a different base or applicator setup is needed, or when it is combined with other ingredients the prescriber chooses.
serious: Get medical help right away for fever, chills, belly or pelvic pain, foul-smelling discharge, or signs of an allergic reaction such as hives or trouble breathing.
interactions: Little terconazole is absorbed, so drug interactions are unlikely, but the cream base may weaken latex condoms and diaphragms during use. Give your prescriber a full list of medicines and supplements.
pregnancy: Avoid vaginal terconazole in the first trimester and use it later in pregnancy only if your prescriber advises; talk to your prescriber if you are pregnant, planning pregnancy or breastfeeding.
tips: Insert it at bedtime and lie down afterward to help it stay in place.
Keep using it through your period and for the full course, even if itching stops sooner.
Wear a panty liner if needed, and avoid tampons, douches and intercourse during treatment.
monitoring: Routine monitoring is usually not needed, but keep follow-up visits your prescriber schedules, and see your prescriber if symptoms come back often.
faqs: How fast does terconazole relieve symptoms?
Many people feel better within a few days, but finish the full course to clear the infection.
Can I use terconazole during my period?
Yes, keep using it as directed. Use pads rather than tampons during treatment.

name: Testosterone
uses: Hormone replacement for men and women with low testosterone, as prescribed and monitored by a clinician.
side: Skin irritation where applied, acne, oily skin, hair growth, mood changes; can transfer to others through skin contact.
how: Replaces or supplements the body's own testosterone, the main male sex hormone that is also present at lower levels in women.
avoid: People with prostate or breast cancer, those who are pregnant or trying to conceive, and people with high red blood cell counts. Keep treated skin away from children, partners and pets.
about: Testosterone is the main male sex hormone, also made in smaller amounts by women. Commercial gels, injections, patches and capsules exist for men with low testosterone, while use in women is off-label in the US. Compounded creams, gels, troches, capsules and other forms let prescribers choose a strength, base or route, such as lower strengths for women, as part of hormone therapy they prescribe and monitor.
serious: Get medical help right away for chest pain, trouble breathing, leg swelling or pain (possible blood clot), signs of a stroke, a painful erection lasting more than 4 hours, or deepening voice and other masculinizing changes in women.
interactions: Testosterone can increase the effect of warfarin and change blood sugar control with insulin or diabetes medicines, and corticosteroids may add to fluid retention. Give your prescriber a full list of medicines and supplements.
pregnancy: Testosterone can harm a developing baby and must not be used in pregnancy or breastfeeding, and pregnant women and children should avoid touching treated skin; talk to your prescriber if you are pregnant, planning pregnancy or breastfeeding.
tips: Apply creams and gels to clean, dry skin at the site your prescriber recommends, let it dry, and cover it with clothing.
Wash your hands with soap after applying, and wash the area before close skin contact with others.
Keep the product away from children and pets, and store it as labeled.
monitoring: Your prescriber will check testosterone levels, blood counts (hematocrit), and often PSA, cholesterol and liver values on a regular schedule.
faqs: How long does testosterone take to work?
Some people notice changes in energy or libido within a few weeks, while other effects can take several months; your prescriber will track your progress.
Can testosterone cream transfer to my partner or pets?
Yes. Cover the application site, wash your hands and the area before contact, and keep children and pets away from treated skin.
Can women use testosterone?
Some prescribers prescribe low doses off-label for women, often for low libido after menopause, with careful monitoring.

name: Tetracaine
uses: Numbing agent in topical anesthetic creams for procedures.
how: Blocks nerve signals to numb the skin.
avoid: Large areas or broken skin; allergy to ester-type numbing agents.
about: Tetracaine is an ester-type local anesthetic that blocks pain signals in nerves. It has been used for decades in eye drops, spinal anesthesia and numbing creams. Prescribers often ask for compounded creams or ointments that combine tetracaine with other numbing agents, such as lidocaine, to numb the skin before cosmetic or minor procedures.
serious: Get medical help right away for dizziness, ringing in the ears, metallic taste, confusion, irregular heartbeat, seizures, blue lips or fingertips, or swelling and trouble breathing.
interactions: Using tetracaine with other numbing products, or over large areas, can add up to toxic levels, and sulfonamide antibiotics may be less effective because of a breakdown product of ester anesthetics. Give your prescriber a full list of medicines and supplements.
pregnancy: Small, short-term skin use is generally considered low risk, but ask before using it in pregnancy or breastfeeding; talk to your prescriber if you are pregnant, planning pregnancy or breastfeeding.
tips: Apply only the amount and area your prescriber directs, and remove it after the time stated.
Do not cover it with plastic wrap or heat unless your prescriber tells you to, since that raises absorption.
Keep numbing creams away from children, and avoid the eyes.
monitoring: Routine monitoring is usually not needed, but keep follow-up visits your prescriber schedules.
faqs: How long does tetracaine take to numb skin?
Numbing often starts within about 30 to 60 minutes after application, depending on the formula and skin area.
Why combine tetracaine with lidocaine?
The two numbing agents work over slightly different times, and prescribers often combine them for procedures.
Is it safe to use numbing cream over a large area?
No, not without direct medical guidance. Large areas or long times can lead to serious side effects.

name: Tetracycline
uses: Bacterial infections, including vet ear preparations.
how: An antibiotic that stops bacteria from making proteins.
avoid: Children under 8 and pregnancy.
about: Tetracycline is one of the original broad-spectrum antibiotics, introduced in the 1950s. It stops many bacteria from building proteins they need to grow. Commercial products are now limited, and newer relatives like doxycycline and minocycline are used more often, but veterinarians may ask for compounded tetracycline in ear packs that also contain other ingredients for ear infections in dogs.
serious: Get medical or veterinary help right away for severe headache with vision changes, a blistering rash, yellow skin or eyes, severe diarrhea, or signs of an allergic reaction.
interactions: By mouth, tetracycline binds calcium, dairy, iron, magnesium, zinc and antacids, which block its absorption, and it may increase the effect of warfarin; ear products have little absorption. Give your prescriber, or your pet's veterinarian, a full list of medicines, supplements and flea or tick products.
pregnancy: Tetracycline is avoided in pregnancy and breastfeeding because it can stain a baby's developing teeth and affect bone growth; talk to your prescriber if you are pregnant, planning pregnancy or breastfeeding.
petNotes: Ear packs are placed in the ear canal by the veterinarian and slowly release medicine for days. Do not clean or flush the ears afterward unless your vet tells you to.
tips: Keep your dog from scratching or shaking the head too hard right after an ear pack is placed, if possible.
Follow your veterinarian's instructions about when to return for a recheck.
Oral tetracycline should be taken on an empty stomach with water, away from dairy.
monitoring: Your veterinarian will usually recheck the ears at a follow-up visit to make sure the infection is clearing.
faqs: What is an ear pack?
An ear pack is a gel-like medicine placed deep in the ear canal by a veterinarian. It releases medicine over days so you don't need to give daily ear drops.
Why can't children under 8 take tetracycline?
It can permanently stain developing teeth, so it is usually avoided in young children.

name: Theophylline
uses: Bronchodilator for asthma and airway disease; also an ingredient in topical sexual-health creams.
how: Relaxes airway muscles and increases blood flow; topically it is used for its circulation effects.
avoid: People with heart rhythm problems, seizures or stomach ulcers (oral use). Oral forms interact with many medicines.
about: Theophylline is a methylxanthine bronchodilator, related to caffeine, that relaxes airway muscles. It has been used for asthma and chronic lung disease for many decades, though inhalers are now usually used first. Veterinarians use it off-label for airway disease in dogs and cats, and prescribers may ask for compounded slow-release capsules or flavored suspensions, or creams that use it topically off-label.
serious: Get medical or veterinary help right away for repeated vomiting, a very fast or irregular heartbeat, seizures, severe restlessness or confusion, which may be signs of too much theophylline.
interactions: Many medicines can raise theophylline levels, including ciprofloxacin, enrofloxacin, erythromycin, cimetidine, fluvoxamine and allopurinol, while smoking, rifampin and some seizure medicines can lower them; limit caffeine. Give your prescriber, or your pet's veterinarian, a full list of medicines, supplements and flea or tick products.
pregnancy: Theophylline may be used in pregnancy when needed, though blood levels can change, and it passes into breast milk and may make a nursing baby irritable; talk to your prescriber if you are pregnant, planning pregnancy or breastfeeding.
petNotes: Dogs and cats process theophylline differently, so doses are species-specific. Watch for vomiting, restlessness or a racing heart, and avoid fluoroquinolone antibiotics unless your vet adjusts the dose.
tips: Do not crush or open slow-release capsules.
Take it the same way each day, consistently with or without food.
Limit caffeine from coffee, tea, soda and chocolate, which can add to side effects.
monitoring: With oral theophylline, your prescriber may check theophylline blood levels, especially when starting, changing the dose or adding medicines.
faqs: Why does theophylline need blood level checks?
The safe range is narrow, and many medicines and conditions change its level, so blood tests help keep it in range.
Can I drink coffee while taking theophylline?
Caffeine is closely related to theophylline and can add to nervousness and fast heartbeat, so limit it and ask your prescriber.

name: Thiamine (vitamin B1)
uses: Vitamin B1 supplement.
how: Vitamin B1, needed for nerve and energy metabolism.
avoid: Usually well tolerated.
about: Thiamine, or vitamin B1, is a water-soluble vitamin the body needs to turn food into energy and to keep nerves, heart and brain working normally. Deficiency can occur with poor diet, heavy alcohol use, some medical conditions and, in pets, certain raw fish diets or improperly made foods. Prescribers and veterinarians may ask for compounded capsules in a specific strength or without fillers a patient cannot tolerate.
conditions: Vitamin B1 support with alcohol use disorder
serious: Get medical or veterinary help right away for signs of an allergic reaction such as hives, swelling or trouble breathing, or for confusion, wobbly walking or eye movement changes that suggest severe deficiency.
interactions: Thiamine has few known drug interactions; long-term diuretic use (such as furosemide) may lower thiamine levels. Give your prescriber, or your pet's veterinarian, a full list of medicines, supplements and flea or tick products.
pregnancy: Thiamine is a normal nutrient that is needed in pregnancy and breastfeeding, and supplements are generally considered safe at recommended amounts; talk to your prescriber if you are pregnant, planning pregnancy or breastfeeding.
petNotes: Cats are especially sensitive to thiamine deficiency, which can cause head tilting, wobbliness, curling of the neck or seizures and needs urgent vet care. Diets heavy in raw fish can destroy thiamine.
tips: Take or give it with or without food as directed.
Store capsules away from heat and moisture.
Tell your prescriber or veterinarian about diet changes, since diet strongly affects B1 needs.
monitoring: Routine monitoring is usually not needed, but keep follow-up visits your prescriber or veterinarian schedules.
faqs: Can you take too much thiamine?
Extra thiamine is usually passed in the urine, so oral thiamine is generally well tolerated, but follow the amount prescribed.
Why is thiamine important for cats?
Cats need more thiamine than dogs and can develop serious nerve signs quickly when they don't get enough.

name: Thyroid (desiccated)
uses: Natural thyroid hormone replacement.
how: Dried thyroid gland that contains both T4 and T3 hormones.
avoid: People with heart disease or untreated adrenal insufficiency.
about: Desiccated thyroid is dried, powdered thyroid gland, usually from pigs, that contains both T4 and T3 thyroid hormones. It was the main thyroid treatment for decades before synthetic levothyroxine became common, and some people and prescribers still prefer it. Compounded capsules, including slow-release capsules, let a prescriber order a specific strength or avoid fillers or dyes found in commercial tablets.
conditions: Low thyroid after surgery or radioactive iodine
serious: Get medical help right away for chest pain, a racing or irregular heartbeat, shortness of breath, severe headache, or signs of an allergic reaction.
interactions: Calcium, iron, antacids, sucralfate, cholestyramine, soy and high-fiber meals can block absorption, and thyroid hormone can change the effect of warfarin and diabetes medicines. Give your prescriber a full list of medicines and supplements.
pregnancy: Thyroid hormone is continued in pregnancy and breastfeeding, but needs often change, so tell your prescriber right away if you become pregnant or are planning pregnancy.
tips: Take it at the same time each day, usually on an empty stomach with water.
Separate it from calcium, iron and antacids by at least four hours.
Avoid switching between thyroid products without telling your prescriber, since strengths are not always interchangeable.
monitoring: Your prescriber will check thyroid blood tests (such as TSH, free T4 and free T3) several weeks after starting or changing the dose and periodically after that.
faqs: What is the difference between desiccated thyroid and levothyroxine?
Levothyroxine contains only synthetic T4, while desiccated thyroid contains both T4 and T3 from animal glands. Your prescriber decides which fits.
Is desiccated thyroid suitable for vegetarians?
No. It is made from animal thyroid glands, usually from pigs.
How long until I feel a dose change?
It can take several weeks for symptoms and blood tests to settle after a change, which is why labs are usually rechecked after about six weeks.

name: Tinidazole
uses: Parasitic and anaerobic infections.
how: Damages DNA in anaerobic bacteria and some parasites.
avoid: Pregnancy (early) and alcohol use.
about: Tinidazole is a nitroimidazole antimicrobial related to metronidazole that treats certain parasites and anaerobic bacteria. It has been used in the US since 2004 for giardiasis, amebiasis, trichomoniasis and bacterial vaginosis. Veterinarians may use it off-label for Giardia and some other infections in dogs and cats, and a flavored suspension helps mask its strong bitter taste.
serious: Get medical or veterinary help right away for seizures, numbness or tingling in the hands or feet, wobbliness, a severe rash, or signs of an allergic reaction.
interactions: Do not drink alcohol during treatment and for at least 3 days after, and use caution with warfarin, lithium, disulfiram and some seizure medicines. Give your prescriber, or your pet's veterinarian, a full list of medicines, supplements and flea or tick products.
pregnancy: Tinidazole is avoided in the first trimester and generally in breastfeeding (pumping and discarding milk may be advised for a few days); talk to your prescriber if you are pregnant, planning pregnancy or breastfeeding.
petNotes: Tinidazole is very bitter, and pets may drool or foam at the mouth if they taste it, so flavored suspensions help. Watch for wobbliness or unusual eye movements and call your vet.
tips: Take or give it with food to reduce stomach upset.
Shake the suspension well before measuring.
Finish the full course even if symptoms improve.
monitoring: Routine lab monitoring is usually not needed, but your prescriber or veterinarian may recheck a stool or other test to confirm the infection has cleared.
faqs: Why can't I drink alcohol with tinidazole?
Alcohol can cause flushing, nausea, vomiting, headache and a fast heartbeat with tinidazole, so avoid it during treatment and for at least 3 days after.
What is the difference between tinidazole and metronidazole?
They are closely related. Tinidazole lasts longer in the body, so courses can be shorter; your prescriber chooses which fits.

name: Topiramate
uses: Seizures and migraine prevention.
side: Tingling, drowsiness, word-finding difficulty, taste changes.
how: Calms nerve activity through several pathways, including sodium channels and GABA.
avoid: People with kidney stones, glaucoma, or who are pregnant.
about: Topiramate is an anticonvulsant used since the late 1990s to control several types of seizures and to help prevent migraine headaches. It calms overactive nerve signaling in more than one way. A prescriber may ask for compounded capsules when a person needs a strength that commercial tablets or capsules don't provide, has trouble swallowing, or needs to avoid certain fillers or dyes.
serious: Get medical help right away for sudden eye pain or blurred vision, decreased sweating with fever, severe confusion, thoughts of suicide, a severe rash, kidney stone pain or blood in the urine, or fast breathing with extreme tiredness.
interactions: Topiramate can make hormonal birth control less effective, and use caution with other seizure medicines, carbonic anhydrase inhibitors (such as acetazolamide), metformin, lithium, alcohol and other sedating medicines. Give your prescriber a full list of medicines and supplements.
pregnancy: Topiramate can raise the risk of cleft lip or palate and other problems in a developing baby; talk to your prescriber if you are pregnant, planning pregnancy or breastfeeding, and do not stop it on your own.
tips: Drink plenty of water throughout the day to help prevent kidney stones.
Do not stop it suddenly, as seizures may increase; your prescriber will taper it.
Avoid alcohol and use care driving until you know how it affects you.
monitoring: Your prescriber may check bicarbonate (blood acid levels) and kidney function, and will follow seizure or headache frequency.
faqs: How long does topiramate take to prevent migraines?
Doses are usually increased slowly, and it may take several weeks to a few months to judge how well it works.
Why does topiramate cause tingling?
Tingling in the hands, feet or face is a common effect of its action on nerves and often eases over time. Tell your prescriber if it is bothersome.
Can topiramate affect birth control?
Yes, it can make hormonal birth control less effective, so talk with your prescriber about the best method.

name: Torsemide
uses: Fluid buildup from heart failure.
how: A long-acting loop diuretic that makes the kidneys remove more salt and water.
avoid: People or pets who are dehydrated or have low potassium; needs kidney monitoring.
about: Torsemide is a loop diuretic that works in the kidney to remove extra salt and water from the body. It has been used since the 1990s for fluid buildup from heart failure, kidney disease and liver disease, and it acts longer than furosemide. Veterinarians use it off-label for congestive heart failure in dogs and cats, and a flavored suspension helps with small or hard-to-pill pets.
conditions: Edema from kidney or liver disease
serious: Get medical or veterinary help right away for extreme thirst or dry mouth, very little urine, muscle cramps or weakness, fainting, confusion, or a fast or irregular heartbeat.
interactions: Use caution with NSAIDs, other diuretics, ACE inhibitors, digoxin, lithium and aminoglycoside antibiotics, which can affect kidney function, potassium or hearing. Give your prescriber, or your pet's veterinarian, a full list of medicines, supplements and flea or tick products.
pregnancy: Torsemide is used in pregnancy only when clearly needed, and its effects in breastfeeding are not well known; talk to your prescriber if you are pregnant, planning pregnancy or breastfeeding.
petNotes: Pets on torsemide drink and urinate more, so always leave fresh water out and give extra potty breaks. Counting resting breathing rate at home helps your vet track heart failure.
tips: Morning dosing helps avoid nighttime urination.
Shake the suspension well and measure each dose carefully.
Do not limit water unless your prescriber or veterinarian tells you to.
monitoring: Your prescriber or veterinarian will check kidney function and electrolytes such as potassium and sodium, especially after starting or changing the dose.
faqs: What is the difference between torsemide and furosemide?
Both are loop diuretics. Torsemide lasts longer and is absorbed more consistently, so some patients switch; your prescriber decides.
How do I count my pet's resting breathing rate?
While your pet sleeps, count breaths (each rise of the chest) for 30 seconds and double it. Tell your vet if it rises above the limit they gave you.

name: Tranexamic acid
uses: Brightening creams for dark spots and melasma; bleeding control.
how: Blocks plasmin, an enzyme involved in bleeding and in pigment production.
avoid: People with a history of blood clots (oral forms).
about: Tranexamic acid is an antifibrinolytic that helps blood clots stay in place by blocking plasmin. It has long been used by mouth or injection for heavy menstrual bleeding and to reduce bleeding with surgery or dental work. Dermatologists also use it off-label in creams for melasma and dark spots, and veterinarians may use it off-label for bleeding control, so compounded creams and flavored suspensions may be requested.
conditions: Dark spots and uneven skin tone
Bleeding control after dental or surgical procedures
serious: Get medical or veterinary help right away for signs of a blood clot such as leg pain or swelling, chest pain, sudden shortness of breath, or sudden weakness, vision change or trouble speaking.
interactions: With oral use, avoid combining with hormonal birth control or other products that raise clot risk unless your prescriber approves; topical creams have few known interactions. Give your prescriber, or your pet's veterinarian, a full list of medicines, supplements and flea or tick products.
pregnancy: Topical use is minimally absorbed, and oral use in pregnancy and breastfeeding is decided case by case; talk to your prescriber if you are pregnant, planning pregnancy or breastfeeding.
petNotes: In dogs, tranexamic acid is used off-label for bleeding, and high doses can cause vomiting. Use only the pet dose your veterinarian prescribes.
tips: Apply the cream to clean, dry skin as directed, and wear sunscreen every day, since sun worsens melasma.
Results on dark spots often take two to three months of regular use.
Shake the oral suspension well before measuring each dose.
monitoring: Routine monitoring is usually not needed for topical use, but your prescriber or veterinarian may follow up with exams or blood tests during oral treatment.
faqs: How long does tranexamic acid cream take to fade dark spots?
Many people need consistent use for about two to three months to see a change, along with daily sunscreen.
Can I use tranexamic acid cream with other brightening products?
It is often combined with other ingredients, but adding products can raise irritation; ask your prescriber before mixing.

name: Trazodone
uses: Sleep and anxiety in people; calming before vet visits, travel and recovery in dogs and cats.
side: Drowsiness, low blood pressure, stomach upset.
how: Blocks certain serotonin receptors and has a calming, sleep-promoting effect.
avoid: People or pets taking other serotonin medicines, and those with heart rhythm problems.
about: Trazodone is an antidepressant first approved in the early 1980s that is now widely prescribed in lower doses off-label to help with sleep. Veterinarians use it off-label to calm dogs and cats before vet visits, travel and grooming, and to keep pets quiet during recovery after surgery. Compounded flavored liquids, treats and transdermal gels help with pets that refuse pills or need a smaller dose.
conditions: Vet visit and travel anxiety in dogs and cats
Cage rest after surgery in dogs
serious: Get medical or veterinary help right away for fainting, a fast or irregular heartbeat, a painful erection lasting more than 4 hours, high fever with muscle stiffness or shaking, unusual bleeding, or new thoughts of suicide.
interactions: Avoid MAO inhibitors (including selegiline and amitraz in pets), and use caution with SSRIs, some opioid pain medicines, triptans and other serotonin medicines, sedatives, alcohol, QT-prolonging drugs and blood thinners. Give your prescriber, or your pet's veterinarian, a full list of medicines, supplements and flea or tick products.
pregnancy: Trazodone is used in pregnancy and breastfeeding only when the benefits outweigh the risks; talk to your prescriber if you are pregnant, planning pregnancy or breastfeeding.
petNotes: For vet visits, it is often given a set time beforehand, and a trial dose at home first helps you see how your pet responds. Some pets may become wobbly or, rarely, more excited.
tips: For sleep, take it shortly before bedtime, and a light snack may reduce dizziness.
For pets, give a test dose on a calm day before the vet visit or trip, as your veterinarian directs.
Wear gloves when applying transdermal gel to your pet's ear, and rotate ears.
monitoring: Routine lab monitoring is usually not needed, but keep follow-up visits, and your prescriber may check an ECG if you have heart rhythm concerns.
faqs: How long before a vet visit should I give trazodone?
Veterinarians often suggest giving it about one to two hours before the visit, but follow the timing on your pet's label.
Can I drink alcohol with trazodone?
No. Alcohol adds to drowsiness and dizziness and should be avoided.
Is trazodone addictive?
It is not considered habit-forming, but stopping a long-term dose suddenly may cause unpleasant symptoms, so ask your prescriber how to stop.

name: Tretinoin
uses: Acne, sun damage, fine lines and dark spots.
side: Dryness, peeling, sun sensitivity. Avoid in pregnancy.
how: A vitamin A derivative that speeds skin cell turnover and unclogs pores.
avoid: Pregnancy. Increases sun sensitivity.
about: Tretinoin is a topical retinoid, a form of vitamin A, that has been used for acne since the early 1970s and later for sun-damaged and aging skin. It increases skin cell turnover and supports collagen. Prescribers may ask for compounded creams, gels or serums to choose a specific strength, a gentler base, or a combination with ingredients such as niacinamide or hyaluronic acid.
serious: Get medical help right away for severe blistering, crusting or swelling of the skin, or signs of an allergic reaction such as hives or trouble breathing.
